findings: Three to five peers. A1 Bulgaria is a direct peer for Vivacom across mobile, fixed broadband, TV, entertainment, business ICT and IoT. A1 was founded in 1994, acquired by Telekom Austria Group in 2005, and A1 Group says it is second-largest in mobile and fixed-line segments and overall number one in the market (https://a1.com/a1-group-and-markets/a1-in-bulgaria/).

Three to five peers. A1's predecessor Mobiltel was bought by Telekom Austria in a 2005 transaction valued at up to EUR 1.6 billion. A1 later bought STEMO, with SeeNews citing industry sources that put the price around BGN 50 million, equal to about EUR 25.6 million (https://www.novinite.com/articles/48248/Telekom%2BAustria%2BAcquires%2BBulgaria%27s%2BMobiltel; https://seenews.com/news/a1-bulgaria-closes-buy-of-local-stemo-in-boost-to-corporate-it-services-1214760).

Three to five peers. Yettel Bulgaria is a direct peer for Vivacom in mobile, fixed wireless broadband and TV. It started as Globul in 2001, was sold by OTE to Telenor in 2013 for EUR 717 million, was bought as part of Telenor's CEE assets by PPF in 2018 for EUR 2.8 billion, and is now owned by e& PPF Telecom Group (https://www.telekom.com/en/media/media-information/archive/greece-ote-agrees-to-sell-globul-for-717-million-to-telenor-358962; https://en.yettel.hu/press/press-release/ppf-group-completes-acquisiton; https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria).

Three to five peers. Yettel's current parent was formed after e& bought control of PPF Telecom assets outside Czechia, with the announced consideration at EUR 2.15 billion plus a possible earn-out of up to EUR 350 million. The European Commission conditionally approved the acquisition under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation on 24 September 2024 (https://en.yettel.hu/press/press-release/ppf-group-press-release-ppf-closes-a-major-transaction-and-forms-a-partnership-with-e-a-global-technology-group; https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/en/ip_24_4842/IP_24_4842_EN.pdf).

Three to five peers. Neterra is a narrower peer for Vivacom's enterprise, wholesale, satellite, cloud, data-center and managed-service audiences. Neterra was founded in 1996 in Sofia, owns and operates four data centers and a global network of over 220 points of presence, according to SeeNews (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-neterra-invests-12-mln-euro-in-data-network-upgrade-1289377).

Three to five peers. Neterra's own history says it built the first Bulgarian alternative connection to Turkey, created a Frankfurt point of presence, launched a large DWDM optical network in Bulgaria and operates Neterra.TV for Bulgarians abroad. CRC data places Neterra among the leading leased-line undertakings, which makes it a real B2B choice even if it is not a national mass-market mobile operator (https://neterra.net/about-us; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

How each peer positions and communicates. A1 positions as a full-service market leader. Its own description covers communications, payment, entertainment, mobile, fixed, broadband, satellite TV, its interactive TV platform, MAX Sport, financial services, ICT, cloud and IoT (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594).

How each peer positions and communicates. A1 communicates by splitting channels by role. In Q1 2026, Pikasa found A1 used Facebook for sports and occasions, LinkedIn for 5G projects, network awards and its internal academy, and YouTube for self-service tutorials (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

How each peer positions and communicates. Yettel positions around certified network quality and customer trust. Its owner says Yettel's network reaches over 99% of the population and has nine umlaut Best in Test certificates; SeeNews reports one such certificate at 926 points out of 1,000, first in reliability, coverage, voice and latency (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria; https://seenews.com/news/seventh-consecutive-best-in-test-certificate-outlines-yettels-network-as-the-best-1254822).

How each peer positions and communicates. Yettel communicates through employer, sustainability and original content themes. Pikasa found its strongest platform was LinkedIn, supported by CEO transition announcements, Top Employer certification and intern programme content (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

How each peer positions and communicates. Neterra positions as an enterprise and carrier-grade connectivity provider. Its homepage sells Enterprise Internet with 99.99% uptime, seven-day rapid deployment and 24/7 expert support, while its services list covers business internet, backup internet, Starlink satellite internet, dedicated internet, NetIX, colocation, cloud, DDoS protection and audio-video services (https://neterra.net/).

How each peer positions and communicates. Neterra communicates through infrastructure proof and customer quotes. Its site cites over 75 countries of network presence, European industry memberships, awards, data centers, NetIX traffic records and testimonials from the National Palace of Culture, WebIT foundation and Unimasters Logistic (https://neterra.net/about-us; https://neterra.net/).

Each peer's narrative. A1's narrative is breadth plus market scale: mobile, fixed, TV, sport, payment, ICT, cloud and IoT under one provider. A1 calls itself "overall, the number one in the market"; CRC corroborates A1 as the largest mobile voice operator by subscribers, but CRC shows Vivacom leading fixed internet and pay-TV, so the self-claim is segment-dependent (https://a1.com/a1-group-and-markets/a1-in-bulgaria/; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Each peer's narrative. A1 also runs a challenger-regulator narrative against Vivacom concentration. It says Vivacom acquisitions could create a dominant TV and broadband player, and CRC later shows Vivacom's 2024 pay-TV share near 60% after Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria were incorporated (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Each peer's narrative. Yettel's narrative is mobile quality, reliability and employer credibility. Yettel calls itself the "largest mobile telecommunications provider in Bulgaria by revenue"; CRC corroborates that Yettel held the highest 2024 retail mobile voice revenue share at 40.9% (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Each peer's narrative. Yettel also publishes a human-use narrative around accessibility, digital literacy, volunteering, sustainability content and original YouTube series. Pikasa says this gave Yettel the most genuinely varied media coverage among the three national operators in Q1 2026 (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

Each peer's narrative. Neterra's narrative is business-grade infrastructure rather than mass consumer telecom. It says its mission is to empower customers everywhere through information technology and customer care, and CRC corroborates its business-network role through a 10.4% share of retail leased lines by line count and a 33.7% share of wholesale leased-line revenue in 2024 (https://neterra.net/about-us; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

What each peer publishes to be known for. A1 publishes to be known for full-service breadth and market leadership. It lists mobile and fixed services, broadband, satellite TV, interactive TV, MAX Sport, financial services, ICT, cloud and IoT, and A1 Group reports EUR 821 million revenue for Bulgaria in 2024 (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594; https://a1.com/a1-group-and-markets/a1-in-bulgaria/).

What each peer publishes to be known for. A1 publishes to be known for ICT leadership after the STEMO deal. A1 said STEMO would help it become the ICT market leader in Bulgaria, and SeeNews reports the acquisition was completed in August 2022 after competition approval (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-telekom-austria-group-announces-100-acquisition-of-stemo-a-bulgarian-ict-company?id=158471&l=english&menueid=14594; https://seenews.com/news/a1-bulgaria-closes-buy-of-local-stemo-in-boost-to-corporate-it-services-1214760).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Yettel publishes to be known for certified network quality. It cites nine Best in Test certificates from umlaut, and SeeNews reports Yettel scored 926 out of 1,000 in one 2024 umlaut test across Bulgaria (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria; https://seenews.com/news/seventh-consecutive-best-in-test-certificate-outlines-yettels-network-as-the-best-1254822).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Yettel publishes to be known as an employer and social-impact operator. Its owner says it is the first and only Bulgarian telecom certified as a Top Employer, and Pikasa reports Yettel coverage around tactile strips, digital literacy reaching 60,000 children, volunteering culture, Super People and sustainability content (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria; https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Neterra publishes to be known for global connectivity, business internet, cloud, colocation, DDoS protection, satellite and NetIX. Its site says it has a network in over 75 countries, and SeeNews reports a EUR 12 million optical data network upgrade in 2026 using Infinera equipment from Nokia (https://neterra.net/about-us; https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-neterra-invests-12-mln-euro-in-data-network-upgrade-1289377).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Neterra publishes to be known for awards and critical infrastructure. Its history lists Best CEE Connectivity Provider awards, NetIX traffic above 4 Tbps, a second Sofia data-center building and DDoS protection for the Bulgarian Presidency of the EU Council (https://neterra.net/about-us).

Each peer's share of voice. A1 had the largest social voice in Pikasa's Q1 2026 telecom dataset: 277 posts, 48,682 total engagements and 176 average engagements per post. A1 had 137 press articles in the same dataset (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

Each peer's share of voice. A1's business voice is large. A1 Group reports 2024 Bulgaria revenue of EUR 821 million, EBITDA of EUR 341 million and CAPEX of EUR 121 million (https://a1.com/a1-group-and-markets/a1-in-bulgaria/).

Each peer's share of voice. Yettel had the smallest social footprint in Pikasa's Q1 2026 dataset: 115 posts, 4,870 total engagements and 42 average engagements per post. Yettel had 157 press articles and the most genuine media coverage of the three operators in that analysis (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

Each peer's share of voice. Yettel's business voice is smaller than A1 but strong in mobile. It reports 2025 revenue of EUR 557 million, EBITDA of EUR 162 million, 3.208 million mobile subscribers, 141,000 fixed broadband subscribers and 104,000 pay-TV subscribers (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria).

Each peer's share of voice. Neterra's voice is strongest in enterprise connectivity measures rather than mass media. CRC reports Neterra held 10.4% of retail leased lines by line count, 8.4% of retail leased-line revenue, 25.9% of wholesale leased lines by line count and 33.7% of wholesale leased-line revenue in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

The white space. The main national operators converge on network, technology, entertainment, ESG and employer claims. The supplied brief already flags that sameness, and the public record supports it through A1's market-scale and service-breadth claims, Yettel's certified network-quality claims and Vivacom's fibre, 5G and TV growth frame (SOURCE DOCUMENT: sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md; https://a1.com/a1-group-and-markets/a1-in-bulgaria/; https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/yettel-bulgaria; https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/).

The white space. A less occupied space is a national digital-infrastructure story that connects scale to people's daily and economic progress, not only to network claims. Vivacom has the assets for that story, but Pikasa's Q1 2026 analysis says much of its press volume was PR-led announcements with weak audience response (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war; SOURCE DOCUMENT: sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md).

The white space. Another open space is useful public service content. Pikasa says Yettel earned more varied coverage from tactile strips, digital literacy reaching 60,000 children, volunteering culture and entertainment stories, while A1 and Vivacom were more often present through sponsorship, product or announcement material (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war).

The white space. A B2B white space sits between mass telecom and specialist infrastructure. A1 owns ICT breadth through STEMO, Neterra owns enterprise-network credibility, and Vivacom can credibly connect national network scale with smart cities, cybersecurity, education, EON and fibre if it proves the role through named projects (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-telekom-austria-group-announces-100-acquisition-of-stemo-a-bulgarian-ict-company?id=158471&l=english&menueid=14594; https://neterra.net/about-us; https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/).

Vivacom origin. Vivacom was Bulgarian Telecommunications Company before the entity was renamed Vivacom Bulgaria EAD after 30 years using the BTC name. Its roots are the former state fixed-line operator, and this history explains why former-monopoly framing is a live positioning risk (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivacom; SOURCE DOCUMENT: sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md). (bears on: Business problem / organizational objective)

Vivacom privatization. Viva Ventures, linked to Advent International, bought 65% of BTC in 2004 for EUR 230 million and paid another EUR 50 million for a mobile licence. A separate company profile gives the 65% sale price as EUR 275.356 million, so the precise privatization figure should be checked before client use (https://euobserver.com/88022/bulgarias-phone-company-from-state-to-private-monopoly; https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525). (bears on: Business problem / organizational objective)

Vivacom current ownership. United Group agreed in 2019 to acquire Vivacom, and the 2020 closing was reported as a EUR 1.2 billion acquisition of Bulgarian Telecommunications Company EAD. United Group says Vivacom has been part of United Group since 2020 (https://www.bcpartners.com/news/bc-partners-owned-united-group-acquires-vivacom/; https://ceelegalmatters.com/bulgaria/14224-united-group-s-acquisition-of-vivacom-closes; https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/). (bears on: Business problem / organizational objective)

Vivacom self-claim verdict. Vivacom's parent presents it as a leading provider of mobile, fixed broadband and television services in Bulgaria. CRC data corroborates leadership in fixed internet subscribers at 39.4% in 2024 and pay-TV subscribers at almost 60%, but not mobile subscriber leadership, where A1 held 36.5% in 2024 (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)

Vivacom growth frame. Vivacom's parent frames the growth story around fibre, 5G and television, and says Bulgaria's market grew close to 5% last year to EUR 2.16 billion. CRC's 2024 report corroborates the same growth areas: fixed internet subscribers rose to 2.643 million, IPTV reached 47.8% of pay-TV subscribers, and Vivacom's fixed internet share rose by 7.2 percentage points (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)

Competition constraint. A1 publicly argued in July 2023 that Vivacom's acquisitions could give it over 60% of TV distribution and nearly 40% of internet. CRC later reported Vivacom at almost 60% of pay-TV subscribers and 37.1% of fixed internet retail revenue in 2024 after Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria were incorporated into Vivacom (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). (bears on: Constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Vivacom communications signal. Pikasa's Q1 2026 analysis says Vivacom led press volume with 198 articles, but most were PR texts with near-zero audience response. It also says Vivacom's strongest social result was Instagram, with 327 average engagements per post, driven by Valentine's Day giveaways and influencer-led EON content (https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)

Three to five peers. A fourth direct peer is CETIN Bulgaria for Vivacom's public-sector, wholesale and network-infrastructure audiences. CETIN Bulgaria was established in July 2020 by separating telecom infrastructure from Telenor Bulgaria. It provides mobile network services for Yettel Bulgaria. Its parent reports 2025 revenue of EUR 170 million, EBITDA of EUR 123 million and CAPEX of EUR 76 million. It won rural digital network contracts alongside A1 and Vivacom under Bulgaria's 2025 BGN 433.6 million programme (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria; https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695).

Three to five peers. The competitive set now reads as four practical choices by audience: A1 and Yettel for national consumer and business telecom, Neterra for enterprise, carrier, cloud and data-center buyers, and CETIN for wholesale and public-infrastructure buyers. This pattern is derived from the banked A1, Yettel and Neterra peer findings plus the CETIN findings in this pass (banked findings; https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria).

How each peer positions and communicates. CETIN positions as infrastructure, not a retail brand. CETIN International's own heading says, "We drive digital transformation by providing cutting-edge communication infrastructure solutions". Its profile says it serves anchor tenants and other telecom providers. Its Bulgaria page says it provides mobile network services for Yettel. The 2025 government-contract reports corroborate CETIN's infrastructure role by naming it with A1 and Vivacom as an implementation partner, but they do not test the quality claim (https://www.cetin.international/what-we-do/profile; https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria; https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695).

How each peer positions and communicates. Independent network evidence splits performance claims across the three retail operators. Opensignal's January 2026 Bulgaria report says A1 is fastest, Yettel stands out on reliability and time on network, and Vivacom wins coverage awards. That challenges any single operator's unqualified network-leadership wording and pushes claims into narrower language (https://insights.opensignal.com/reports/2026/01/bulgaria/mobile-network-experience).

Each peer's narrative. The peer pattern is acquired scale versus built specialist depth. A1, Yettel and Vivacom are now parts of larger cross-border groups after major transactions, while Neterra's banked history presents a Sofia-founded specialist that built its own international network. This pattern is derived from banked findings: A1 2005 acquisition; Yettel OTE-to-Telenor-to-PPF-to-e& PPF chain; Vivacom United Group acquisition; Neterra founded in Sofia and expanded through network build-out (banked findings).

Each peer's narrative. CETIN's narrative is separated infrastructure serving retail operators. It was created from Telenor Bulgaria's infrastructure in 2020. Its own materials frame the rural broadband project as equal digital access for remote areas. SeeNews corroborates the state programme, the BGN 433.6 million contract value and the A1, Vivacom and CETIN participants (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria; https://www.cetin.international/w/expanding-bulgaria-s-digital-future-with-large-scale-fiber-deployment; https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695).

What each peer publishes to be known for. CETIN publishes to be known for 5G and fibre infrastructure for anchor tenants and telecom providers. Its 2026 case study says the rural programme will connect at least 700 mobile base stations and more than 200 rural settlements in 140+ municipalities. The Sofia Globe and SeeNews corroborate the project and contract value, but not CETIN's own impact wording (https://www.cetin.international/what-we-do/profile; https://www.cetin.international/w/expanding-bulgaria-s-digital-future-with-large-scale-fiber-deployment; https://sofiaglobe.com/2025/06/10/bulgaria-signs-six-contracts-worth-434m-leva-for-digital-connectivity-in-small-settlements/; https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Neterra now publishes to be known for hybrid internet, Starlink resale and backup internet. It says 2025 business internet revenue grew 32%, NetIX subscription revenue grew 43%, and its fibre-backbone work raised capacity on key routes to 800 Gbps per channel. The accessible source for those operating figures in this pass was Neterra; independent corroboration was not found (https://neterra.net/news/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Independent trade coverage corroborates Neterra's awards claim for 2025. AmCham Bulgaria reported that Neterra won Best Central & Eastern European Connectivity Provider for the third year in a row and that NetIX won Best Internet Exchange Provider (https://amcham.bg/2025/10/24/double-victory-for-neterra-and-netix-at-the-capacity-global-connectivity-awards-2025/).

Each peer's share of voice. Capital's 2026 coverage reported 2025 revenue figures of EUR 895.1 million for A1, EUR 776 million for Vivacom and EUR 557 million for Yettel. That makes A1 the largest reported revenue voice in that article, while Yettel remains materially smaller outside mobile-specific measures (https://www.capital.bg/en/business/2026/07/07/4931794_the_telecom_market_three_major_operators_and_over_2/).

Each peer's share of voice. CETIN's business voice is visible in infrastructure accounts rather than retail media. Its parent reports 2025 revenue of EUR 170 million, EBITDA of EUR 123 million and CAPEX of EUR 76 million. CETIN also appears in the 2025 BGN 433.6 million rural network programme with A1 and Vivacom, but no split of that total by operator was found (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria; https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695).

Each peer's share of voice. Neterra's global-exchange voice is larger than its national retail profile. AmCham Bulgaria reported that NetIX recorded 4.67 Tbps peak traffic and 43% year-on-year recurring-service revenue growth. It also reported that Neterra's dedicated internet access revenue rose 32% (https://amcham.bg/2025/10/24/double-victory-for-neterra-and-netix-at-the-capacity-global-connectivity-awards-2025/).

The white space. The banked findings create a claim-tiering white space. A1 can claim breadth and speed; Yettel can claim certified mobile quality and employer trust; Vivacom can claim fixed internet, pay-TV and coverage; Neterra can claim specialist enterprise infrastructure. No player can safely own total leadership without qualifiers. This pattern is derived from the banked A1, Yettel, Vivacom and Neterra share and narrative findings plus Opensignal 2026 (banked findings; https://insights.opensignal.com/reports/2026/01/bulgaria/mobile-network-experience).

The white space. The rural digital-inclusion space is not empty. A1, Vivacom and CETIN all have public claims to the 2025 state-backed rural network build. Vivacom cannot make that story as if it acted alone. The open space is proof of the specific local outcomes Vivacom delivered within the shared programme (https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-signs-222-mln-euro-digital-network-deals-with-a1-vivacom-cetin-1276695; https://www.cetin.international/w/expanding-bulgaria-s-digital-future-with-large-scale-fiber-deployment).

The white space. The wholesale-infrastructure story is occupied by CETIN and Neterra as well as by the retail operators. CETIN owns the separated Yettel network-service role. Neterra owns independent carrier and data-center proof. Vivacom's B2B story must connect national scale to named customer outcomes rather than just say infrastructure (https://www.eandppftelecom.eu/our-companies/cetin-bulgaria; https://amcham.bg/2025/10/24/double-victory-for-neterra-and-netix-at-the-capacity-global-connectivity-awards-2025/).

Competition clearance development. Bulgaria's Supreme Administrative Court issued a final ruling in February 2026 clearing United Group's acquisition of Bulsatcom telecom-infrastructure assets after appeals by A1, Yettel and CETIN. This changes the constraint from unresolved approval risk to a live concentration narrative that competitors can still use publicly (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035). (bears on: Constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Vivacom counter-narrative. In 2023, Broadband TV News reported Vivacom's response to A1 and Yettel allegations. Vivacom called the fixed broadband and pay-TV market a "healthy multi-player environment" and said United Group had invested BGN 3.5 billion, or EUR 1.79 billion, in Bulgaria since entry. This is a self-claim reported by an independent trade outlet; the investment figure was not independently checked in that article (https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2023/07/04/vivacom-dismisses-unfounded-concerns-from-competitors/). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)

Category growth route. Mordor Intelligence estimates Bulgaria's mobile-network-operator market at USD 2.27 billion in 2025 and USD 2.72 billion in 2030. It says data and internet held 44.28% of 2024 revenue and that enterprise spend is forecast to grow faster than consumer spend. This supports the brief's pressure to grow through value and enterprise services, not only consumer volume (https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/bulgaria-telecom-mno-market). (bears on: Business problem / organizational objective)

Three to five peers. The four-peer map still holds. ICLG names A1, Yettel and Vivacom as the mobile operators, names Vivacom and A1 as the main fixed-internet providers, and says the rest of fixed internet is made up of many regional operators. No fifth present nationwide retail peer was established from this source (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

How each peer positions and communicates. Yettel now communicates a broader technology-company position. Its release says it serves more than 3 million customers, offers more than 2,000 products, has 260,000 Home Internet and Yettel TV subscribers, has more than 2 million app downloads and has digitalised 95% of customer interactions. SeeNews reports this as a Yettel press release, so these are company claims carried by an independent outlet, not independently checked there (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-bulgaria-has-invested-eur-1-7-billion-over-25-years-1296648).

How each peer positions and communicates. Neterra and NetIX communicate through rankings, not only infrastructure claims. Neterra's own 2026 Digitalk 101 post says NetIX ranks third among Bulgaria's 50 most efficient information-technology companies, Neterra ranks sixth and NetIX ninth among telecom service providers, and Neterra ranks 45th among information-and-communications-technology exporters. AmCham Bulgaria separately carried the same ranking story, so the publication is corroborated, while the ranking method remains with Digitalk (https://neterra.net/news/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings; https://amcham.bg/2026/08/12/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings/).

Each peer's narrative. Yettel's 25-year anniversary narrative moves beyond certified network quality. It says Globul's 2001 entry brought real competition to Bulgaria. It says Yettel introduced the iPhone in Bulgaria, launched 4G and ran the first public 5G test. It says its strategic direction is to become "more than a telecom". SeeNews labels the item as a Yettel press release, so the source reports the claim but does not independently test it (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-bulgaria-has-invested-eur-1-7-billion-over-25-years-1296648).

Each peer's narrative. The peer pattern is group strength plus local proof. A1 uses service breadth and parent scale. Yettel uses e& PPF ownership, CETIN network support and certified quality. CETIN uses separated infrastructure. Neterra uses its NetIX, data-center and network ecosystem. The pattern means Vivacom's story must show Bulgarian outcomes, not only group scale (banked findings: A1 narrative; Yettel narrative; CETIN narrative; Neterra narrative; Vivacom current ownership).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Yettel publishes to be known for long-term national investment and contribution. It says it has invested EUR 1.7 billion since starting operations in Bulgaria. It says it contributed nearly EUR 350 million to state and municipal budgets in taxes, social security contributions and fees in 2021-2025. SeeNews labels the item as a Yettel press release, so the figures remain company claims in that source (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-bulgaria-has-invested-eur-1-7-billion-over-25-years-1296648).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Yettel publishes to be known for network reach and employer proof. It says 4G reaches 99.75% of the population and 5G reaches 86%. It says Yettel and CETIN invested more than EUR 310 million in the network in 2021-2025. It says it has been Bulgaria's only telecom certified as a Top Employer since 2023 and invested more than EUR 4.1 million in employee training over five years. SeeNews reports these as Yettel release claims, not as independently checked facts (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-bulgaria-has-invested-eur-1-7-billion-over-25-years-1296648).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Neterra publishes to be known for Starlink-linked business continuity. Its 2026 Digitalk 101 post says it became SpaceX's official Starlink distributor, doubled satellite-internet revenue, launched hybrid internet combining Starlink, fibre and 5G, and launched backup internet that switches when the primary link fails. AmCham Bulgaria carried the ranking story, but these operating details remain Neterra's own account in the accessible sources (https://neterra.net/news/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings; https://amcham.bg/2026/08/12/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings/).

Each peer's share of voice. Capital's later August 2026 telecom item says A1 Bulgaria passed EUR 1 billion in 2025 revenue for the first time, followed by Vivacom at EUR 776 million and Yettel at EUR 557 million. Capital's July 2026 item reported A1 at EUR 895.1 million. The A1 2025 figure needs reconciliation before client use (https://www.capital.bg/en/business/2026/08/05/4942699_another_record_year_for_the_bulgarian_telecom_market/; https://www.capital.bg/en/business/2026/07/07/4931794_the_telecom_market_three_major_operators_and_over_2/).

Each peer's share of voice. NetIX's 2026 Digitalk 101 ranking gives Neterra's group a specialist efficiency voice. AmCham Bulgaria reports NetIX at EUR 1.09 million revenue per employee and says it outperformed every telecom operator in that ranking on that measure. This is independent chamber coverage of Neterra and NetIX's published ranking claim (https://amcham.bg/2026/08/12/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings/).

The white space. The open space is not "best network" as a broad claim. SpeedGeo reports Vivacom as fastest fixed broadband in Bulgaria from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026, with 117 Mb/s average download, 85.2 Mb/s upload and 25 ms ping. The same source reports A1 as fastest mobile internet, with 190.7 Mb/s average download. This splits performance proof by service type (https://www.speedgeo.net/statistics/bulgaria).

The white space. A national-infrastructure story must avoid sounding like every peer's proof claim. The banked record shows A1 claiming breadth and speed, Yettel claiming certified quality and trust, Neterra claiming specialist infrastructure, and CETIN claiming wholesale infrastructure. The open space is the human and economic result of the infrastructure, with named local proof (banked findings: A1 narrative; Yettel narrative; Neterra narrative; CETIN narrative; Opensignal 2026 finding).

The white space. The ICLG 2026 Bulgaria chapter says fixed internet has strong infrastructure-based competition and many regional operators outside Vivacom and A1. This leaves room for a local-outcome story by town, school, enterprise or public service, because national share alone does not explain the regional customer experience (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Customer complaint pressure. Bulgaria's Ombudsman reported 525 complaints about telephone, internet and television services in 2024. Vivacom had 187 complaints, Yettel had 164, A1 had 158, and others had 16. The main complaint themes were monthly-fee indexation, unwanted service additions, payment for unused services and service quality. This makes customer fairness a shared category risk, not only a Vivacom issue (https://www.ombudsman.bg/storage/pub/files/20250527115030_ANNUAL%20REPORT%20OMBUDSMAN%202024%20SUMMARY%20EN.pdf). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)

Regulatory frame. The ICLG 2026 Bulgaria chapter lists the Communications Regulation Commission as telecom regulator, the Commission for Protection of Competition as competition enforcer, and the Commission for Personal Data Protection as personal-data authority. It also lists the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Cybersecurity Act, NIS2 and critical-entity resilience rules among laws affecting telecoms and media providers. This supports tight legal review for market, data, cyber and platform claims (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/). (bears on: Constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Three to five peers. No new peer displaced the banked four-peer set. The new sources instead strengthen the same split: A1 and Yettel remain the national retail alternatives, CETIN remains the network-infrastructure peer behind Yettel, and Neterra remains the specialist enterprise and carrier peer (banked findings; https://www.cetinbg.bg/what-we-do/network; https://www.datocms-assets.com/56100/1771365178-fr39_20260217_eand_ppf_telecom_group_fy2025_annual_accounts_public.pdf).

How each peer positions and communicates. A1's current 5G page uses the line "5G ULTRA - истинска 5G технология" and contrasts its 5G ULTRA with 5G DSS. A1 says 5G ULTRA runs on 3.6 GHz spectrum, uses equipment from a European supplier and can exceed 1,000 Mbps. The banked Opensignal and SpeedGeo findings support narrower speed claims for A1, but not an unqualified total-network claim (https://www.a1.bg/5g-ultra; banked Opensignal 2026 finding; banked SpeedGeo finding).

How each peer positions and communicates. CETIN Bulgaria's network page introduces itself as "Your Reliable Partner in Telecommunications and IT Infrastructure". It says Yettel Bulgaria uses CETIN's network solely for all mobile technology, which confirms CETIN communicates as the network behind Yettel rather than as a retail brand (https://www.cetinbg.bg/what-we-do/network).

How each peer positions and communicates. CETIN Bulgaria says its 4G and 5G network covers more than 97% of Bulgarian highways and first- and second-class roads. It says 4G exceeds 99% population coverage and 89% territory coverage, and that 5G has more than 2,750 base stations, with more than 1,000 carrying 5G C-band. These are CETIN claims; the page does not independently test them (https://www.cetinbg.bg/what-we-do/network).

Each peer's narrative. The banked record creates a new ownership pattern: A1, Yettel and Vivacom are foreign-owned converged operators built through major transactions, while Neterra is the Sofia-founded specialist and CETIN is the separated infrastructure company. That means each peer can claim scale, expertise or neutrality from a different origin story, and Vivacom's former-state-operator history remains the only incumbent-origin story in the set (banked findings: A1 acquisition history; Yettel ownership chain; Vivacom origin and current ownership; Neterra origin; CETIN creation).

Each peer's narrative. Yettel's 2026 Code of Conduct adds an ethics-and-responsibility line to its network and employer story. It says, "doing good is good business", and links growth to people, trust and responsibility. This is Yettel's own language; the source does not independently test the claim (https://www.yettel.bg/sites/default/files/2026-08/Yettel_CodeOfConduct_EN.pdf).

Each peer's narrative. Neterra's 2026 content uses a business-continuity story, not only a network-asset story. Its Digitalk 101 article titles one angle "Business Without Geographic Limits" and says hybrid internet combines fibre, 5G, Starlink and other technologies into one service, one device and one contract. This is Neterra's own article; AmCham carried the ranking story, but not every operating detail (https://neterra.net/news/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings; https://amcham.bg/2026/08/12/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings/).

What each peer publishes to be known for. A1 publishes to be known for "5G ULTRA" as "истинска 5G технология". Its 5G page says the network uses 3.6 GHz spectrum and a 100 MHz band, and says download speeds above 1,000 Mbps are already reality. This is A1's own wording; independent sources in the banked record support A1 speed strength but not every technical or comparative claim on the page (https://www.a1.bg/5g-ultra; banked Opensignal 2026 finding; banked SpeedGeo finding).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Yettel publishes to be known for device retail and app-based customer experience. SeeNews carried Yettel's claim that Digitalk 101 ranked it first in the Communications Equipment category from 2023 to 2025, that it offers more than 2,000 products and nearly 200 phone models, and that it sold more than 10 million phones over 25 years. SeeNews labels the item as a Yettel press release (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-leads-mobile-device-and-accessories-sales-for-the-third-consecutive-year-1299605).

What each peer publishes to be known for. CETIN publishes to be known for the fixed-wireless and TV backbone behind Yettel. Its network page says the 5G network acts as the backbone for Fixed Wireless Access and Yettel TV, with up to 300 Mbps service. This is CETIN's own claim; the page does not independently verify the performance statement (https://www.cetinbg.bg/what-we-do/network).

What each peer publishes to be known for. Neterra publishes to be known for hybrid internet and Starlink resale. Its homepage calls Neterra a "Starlink Authorized Reseller" and says its flagship business service combines fibre, Starlink, 5G and other technologies in a single connection. This is Neterra's own wording; independent corroboration in this pass covered the ranking story, not every service claim (https://neterra.net/; https://amcham.bg/2026/08/12/neterra-and-netix-take-leading-positions-in-the-digitalk-101-2026-rankings/).

Each peer's share of voice. A1 Bulgaria reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 438 million, EBITDA of EUR 195 million, EBT of EUR 114 million and CAPEX of EUR 51 million. The same report shows H1 2025 revenue of EUR 404 million, EBITDA of EUR 178 million, EBT of EUR 101 million and CAPEX of EUR 60 million, so A1's Bulgaria business voice was still growing in the first half of 2026 (https://a1.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/07/A1-Group_Half-Year-Financial-Report-2026-1.pdf).

Each peer's share of voice. A1 Bulgaria reported H1 2026 service revenue of EUR 358 million, equipment revenue of EUR 74 million and other operating income of EUR 5 million. That shows most of A1's current reported Bulgaria revenue comes from services, not devices (https://a1.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/07/A1-Group_Half-Year-Financial-Report-2026-1.pdf).

Each peer's share of voice. Yettel Bulgaria had 3.208 million mobile subscribers at 31 December 2025, 85% postpaid share and EUR 13.0 blended mobile ARPU. Its fixed broadband base reached 141.3 thousand subscriptions after 32% annual growth, and pay-TV reached 103.6 thousand subscriptions after 39% annual growth (https://www.datocms-assets.com/56100/1771365178-fr39_20260217_eand_ppf_telecom_group_fy2025_annual_accounts_public.pdf).

Each peer's share of voice. Yettel Bulgaria reported 2025 revenue growth of 3.9% and EBITDA growth of minus 0.6%. Its parent attributed revenue growth mainly to higher ARPU, while fixed broadband growth came through fixed wireless access using CETIN Bulgaria's network (https://www.datocms-assets.com/56100/1771365178-fr39_20260217_eand_ppf_telecom_group_fy2025_annual_accounts_public.pdf).

The white space. The banked record plus new H1 2026 financials sharpen a white space around proof-backed national usefulness. A1 has the stronger current revenue proof, Yettel has mobile customer and employer proof, CETIN has infrastructure proof and Neterra has specialist continuity proof. Vivacom's safer open lane is not another best-network claim, but a named set of Bulgarian outcomes its network made possible (banked findings; https://a1.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/07/A1-Group_Half-Year-Financial-Report-2026-1.pdf; https://www.cetinbg.bg/what-we-do/network; https://www.datocms-assets.com/56100/1771365178-fr39_20260217_eand_ppf_telecom_group_fy2025_annual_accounts_public.pdf).

The white space. The device-and-app space is now more visibly occupied by Yettel. SeeNews carried a Yettel release saying Digitalk 101 ranked Yettel first in mobile device sales for 2023-2025, that smartphone sales through Yettel digital channels rose 56% in H1 2026, and that 95% of customer interactions were digitalised. Vivacom should not use digital customer experience as an ownable centre without proof stronger than Yettel's (https://seenews.com/news/yettel-leads-mobile-device-and-accessories-sales-for-the-third-consecutive-year-1299605).

Vivacom ownership-story risk. SeeNews reported on 18 May 2026 that United Group was considering selling some or all Bulgarian assets, including Vivacom's fixed network and Nova Broadcasting Group. The same article said the report came from local media and that the process was at an early stage. This is a public ownership-story risk, not a confirmed transaction, and should be checked with the client before use (https://seenews.com/news/see-focused-united-group-mulls-selling-bulgarian-assets-report-1294890). (bears on: Constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Employer-reputation comparison. WhereWeWork Bulgaria's 2025 employer ranking placed Yettel Bulgaria first, Vivacom second and A1 Bulgaria third in telecommunications. That makes employer reputation a contested peer field rather than an uncontested Vivacom strength (https://www.wherewework.bg/en/news-and-articles/top-employers-2025-the-most-admired-companies-to-apply-to-in-2026-201). (bears on: Priority audiences & current state)

findings: Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Investors and owners matter because Vivacom is a subsidiary inside United Group. United Group is majority owned by BC Partners and has owned Vivacom since the 2020 closing. United Group says it is active in eight countries, has nearly 16 million users and 15,000 employees, and generated more than EUR 2.7 billion in annual revenue in its 2024 Bulsatcom announcement. (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Owner relations matter because Vivacom sits under a parent with public governance conflict. Economic.bg reported in August 2025 that United Group had a control dispute between founder Dragan Sholak and majority shareholder BC Partners. It reported that Sholak filed a lawsuit after his removal and a dispute over EUR 200 million in bonuses. It also reported market speculation about a possible United Group sale at EUR 8 billion. (https://www.economic.bg/en/a/view/top-management-reshuffle-at-vivacom-director-leaves-spas-rusev-returns)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Communications Regulation Commission matters because it is the national sector regulator and source of market baselines. CRC said Bulgaria's electronic communications market was BGN 4.021 billion in 2024, up 5.7% from 2023. CRC said A1, Vivacom and Yettel formed 97.8% of fixed voice subscribers and 94.0% of fixed voice retail revenue. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. CRC matters for Vivacom's market standing. CRC said Vivacom was the fixed internet leader in 2024 with 39.4% of subscribers and 37.1% of revenue. CRC said Vivacom was the pay TV leader in 2024 with 59.6% of subscribers and 56.5% of revenue after Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria were incorporated into Vivacom. CRC said Vivacom became second in mobile voice revenue in 2024 and its mobile voice revenue share rose from 25.4% in 2020 to 32.0% in 2024. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. CRC matters for public-interest duties. CRC said Vivacom continued to provide public payphones at main entry points and high-traffic places such as airports, ports, railway and bus stations, motorways, hospitals and police stations. CRC said Vivacom continued free calls to emergency numbers from all public payphones. CRC said Vivacom continued tariff packages for low-income users, people with disabilities and people with special social needs. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Commission for Protection of Competition matters because Vivacom's acquisitions have been contested. PPF Telecom Group said CPC approved transactions linked to Networx and Telnet despite court hearings and a court-ordered review. NERA said CPC cleared Vivacom's acquisition of Telnet and Networx unconditionally at Phase 2 on 29 June 2023. (https://www.ppf.eu/en/press-release/ppf-telecom-group-dismayed-by-regulatory-ruling-taken-in-bulgaria; https://www.nera.com/experience/2023/bulgarian-telco-vivacom-cleared-to-acquire-telnet-and-networx-.html)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The European Commission matters for ownership control because United Group said the Vivacom acquisition followed European Commission approval in April 2020. It also matters for earlier history because Vivacom's own history says the 2012 restructuring received approval from the European Commission and other authorities. Company history and former names. Vivacom traces its history to the first Bulgarian communications body created in Pleven in 1879. Vivacom says it is the successor to BTC, Bulgaria's first telecommunications company. In 2004, the state sold 65% of BTC to Viva Ventures, a unit of Advent International; SeeNews records the price as EUR 275.356 million, while Novinite records a widely cited EUR 230 million sale figure. BTC Mobile launched services under the vivatel brand in November 2005. BTC and vivatel combined under the Vivacom brand in 2009. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525; https://www.novinite.com/articles/139418/Bulgaria%2BDefeated%2Bin%2BCourt%2Bby%2BViva%2BVentures%2Bover%2BTelco%2BDeal) (bears on: business and organizational context)

Ownership changes and reported prices. AIG Global Investment Group agreed in 2007 to buy Viva Ventures' 65% BTC stake for EUR 1.08 billion and expected to secure a further 25% stake. Creditor banks were reported in 2012 to have agreed to sell a majority stake in Vivacom for EUR 130 million while debt would be cut to EUR 588 million. VTB Capital secured a majority stake in 2015 for EUR 130 million. United Group agreed in 2019 to acquire Vivacom for a reported EUR 1.2 billion, and the deal closed in 2020. (https://www.rttnews.com/294831/aig-global-investment-group-to-buy-viva-ventures-65-stake-in-bulgarian-telecommunications-for-eur-1-08-bln-update.aspx; https://www.fierce-network.com/europe/banks-agree-to-buy-bulgaria-s-vivacom; https://www.globalprivatecapital.org/newsroom/vtb-capital-to-exit-vivacom-to-bc-partners-backed-united-group-in-usd1-3-billion-acquisition/; https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/) (bears on: decision-maker & approval path)

findings: Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s telecom sector is governed by EU rules including the European Electronic Communications Code, ePrivacy Directive, Net Neutrality Regulation, Roaming Regulation, Gigabit Infrastructure Act and EU termination-rate rules; Bulgarian core laws include the Electronic Communications Act and Electronic Communications Networks and Physical Infrastructure Act (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. Telecom and adjacent digital activity in Bulgaria is also affected by the General Data Protection Regulation, Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Cybersecurity Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, NIS2 Directive and Critical Entity Resilience Directive; this confirms the supplied brief’s legal and AI-policy constraints (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. The Communications Regulation Commission is the independent telecom regulator; the Ministry of Transport and Communications and Ministry of e-Government set ICT, digital administration and cybersecurity policy; the National Radio Frequency Spectrum Council handles national spectrum-planning proposals (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. CRC Decision No. 220 of 30 July 2024 found no effective competition in wholesale access to passive physical infrastructure, named Vivacom as having significant individual impact, and imposed access, non-discrimination, transparency, reference-offer and price-control duties (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC launched a fourth-round analysis of local access at a fixed location, and by Decision No. 251 of 29 August 2025 ordered extra information on fixed access via mobile network for 2021-2023; this keeps fixed access and 5G-based home internet inside active review (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC says Vivacom met all universal-service quality target values in 2024, did not request unfair-burden compensation by the 30 June 2024 statutory deadline, and had a 46% drop in universal-service complaints versus the prior period (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC says 2024 universal-service complaints to Vivacom were mainly technical failures at 27% of complaints; termination complaints rose to 16% from 2% in 2023, and the other category rose 18 percentage points to 29% (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CMS says CRC awarded 20-year 3.6 GHz licences to A1, Vivacom and Yettel in April 2021, and assigned 700 MHz and 800 MHz bands to the same three operators in December 2023 for 15 years; CMS says total licence payments were about BGN 13.4 million (https://cms.law/en/int/expert-guides/cms-expert-guide-to-5g-regulation-and-law/bulgaria).

Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s Supreme Administrative Court issued a final ruling in February 2026 clearing United Group’s acquisition of Bulsatcom telecom infrastructure assets after appeals by A1 Bulgaria, Yettel Bulgaria and Cetin Bulgaria; the court said the deal and base-station infrastructure asset deal were not a notifiable concentration under Bulgarian competition law (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035).

Regulatory context. A1 Group publicly objected in July 2023 to CPC approval of Vivacom acquisitions of Networx-Bulgaria and six smaller operators, saying the deals could give Vivacom more than 60% of TV distribution and nearly 40% of internet; CRC’s 2024 market data later reported Vivacom at 59.6% of pay-TV subscribers and 39.4% of fixed internet subscribers (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

ESG context. United Group says its 2024 sustainability results included 61% electricity from renewable sources, a 52% cut in Scope 1 and 2 emissions against its 2020 baseline, a 13% improvement in its Network Efficiency Index, 25% refurbished customer premises equipment among installed devices, more than 2,300 kg of e-waste recovered, and more than 1,500 smartphones recovered through customer take-back programs (https://united.group/united-group-releases-2024-sustainability-report-highlighting-tangible-progress-across-esg-priorities/).

ESG context. United Group says it is building three solar plants and one wind farm in Bulgaria; by 2027 these assets are planned to supply 160% of electricity needed for the Group’s Bulgarian operations, cover 65% of total Group electricity use, remove about 120,000 tonnes of CO2 from Bulgaria’s grid each year, reach 124 MW combined capacity, and produce 310,000 MWh a year (https://united.group/united-group-enters-renewable-energy-production/).

ESG context. A Vivacom careers page says United Group Energy develops renewable power plants to supply United Group telecom and media operations with 100% green electricity, and says Bulgaria has more than 120 MW of renewable projects under development, construction and operation (https://www.vivacom.bg/bg/residential/za-nas/karieri/obiavi-za-rabota/31166/senior-electrical-engineer-high-voltage-substations-sofia).

ESG context. Vivacom says its management system is certified to ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and ISO/IEC 27018:2019; I did not find an independent certificate register for each standard in this pass, so this is a client claim awaiting document proof (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).

Geopolitical context. United Group is Netherlands-based and majority owned by BC Partners; it completed Vivacom’s acquisition on 31 July 2020 after European Commission approval in April 2020 and a November 2019 agreement (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/).

Geopolitical context. BC Partners said Vivacom had over 1.8 million unique customers at the time of the 2019 acquisition agreement, and described the deal as part of United Group’s expansion from six Southeast European countries (https://www.bcpartners.com/news/bc-partners-owned-united-group-acquires-vivacom/).

Geopolitical context. United Group agreed in February 2025 to sell SBB Serbia to e& PPF Telecom and to sell NetTV Plus and Western Balkan sports rights to Telekom Srbija; the announced combined enterprise value was EUR 1.5 billion, and United Group said the move completed its aim of exiting non-EU telecom assets (https://united.group/united-group-agrees-to-sell-sbb-serbia-as-well-as-net-tv-plus-business-and-its-sports-broadcasting-rights-for-western-balkans/).

Geopolitical context. A May 2026 SeeNews report said United Group was considering selling some or all Bulgarian assets, including Vivacom’s fixed network and Nova Broadcasting Group; the article says the process was early and based on local media reporting, so this is a live ownership-watch item, not a completed event (https://seenews.com/news/see-focused-united-group-mulls-selling-bulgarian-assets-report-1294890).

Geopolitical context. Bulgaria, Kosovo and North Macedonia signed 5G security declarations with the United States on 23 October 2020 under the Clean Network initiative; RFE/RL reported the initiative was aimed at limiting equipment from companies such as Huawei in telecom networks (https://www.rferl.org/a/bulgaria-kosovo-north-macedonia-join-us-initiative-to-block-chinese-equipment-in-5g-network/30909512.html).

Geopolitical context. CRC reported that A1, Vivacom and Yettel provided annual reports in 2024 on their Multivendor Strategy; this makes supplier mix and network security a regulator-visible issue for Vivacom (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. Bulgaria’s electronic communications market reached EUR 2.06 billion in 2024, up 5.7% on 2023, according to the ICLG Bulgaria telecoms chapter citing CRC data (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Category context. United Group said in July 2026 that Bulgaria’s telecom market grew close to 5% last year to EUR 2.16 billion, and said the growth came in fibre, 5G and television (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/).

Category context. CRC reported bundled-service revenue of BGN 2.064 billion in 2024, up 10.6% year on year; A1, Vivacom and Yettel accounted for 97.8% of bundled-service revenue and 98.3% of bundled-service subscribers (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. Vivacom’s bundled-service subscriber share rose from 30.7% in 2023 to 32.9% in 2024, and its bundled-service revenue share rose from 27.6% to 30.2%; CRC says Bulsatcom was deleted from the CRC register and its activity was reported by Vivacom (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. CRC reported retail fixed internet and data-transfer revenue of BGN 1.879791 billion in 2024; Vivacom led retail fixed internet access with 39.4% of subscribers and 37.1% of revenue, up 7.2 and 8.3 percentage points year on year (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. CRC reported 2.02 million pay-TV subscribers at the end of 2024; Vivacom led pay TV with 59.6% of subscribers and 56.5% of revenue after the incorporation of Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. CRC reported IPTV subscribers grew 9.4% in 2024 and IPTV reached 47.8% of pay-TV subscribers; Vivacom, A1 and Yettel together made up 95.0% of IPTV subscribers (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Category context. CRC reported satellite TV subscribers fell 8.4% in 2024; after Bulsatcom was incorporated into Vivacom, Vivacom’s satellite-TV subscriber share exceeded 80.0% by the end of 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Self-claim verdict: 5G coverage. Vivacom says it has the "5G мрежата с най-голямо покритие в България" and that its 5G covers 92% of Bulgaria’s population; CMS confirms Vivacom has extensive 5G coverage but does not rank it first, so the ranking claim needs proof before use (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://cms.law/en/int/expert-guides/cms-expert-guide-to-5g-regulation-and-law/bulgaria). (bears on: reputation problem / desired perception)

Self-claim verdict: fibre speed. Vivacom says it has the fastest fixed fibre network for home internet in Bulgaria as of 23 May 2025 based on CRC’s tariff comparison tool; nPerf’s public awards page confirms a 2024 Bulgaria fixed-line performance award page exists, but the page opened in this pass did not expose the winner text, so the claim needs the CRC comparison record or nPerf report before it is used as a fact (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://www.nperf.com/en/awards/bg/2024/broadband/bulgaria). (bears on: reputation problem / desired perception)

Platform dependency. United Group selected Eutelsat as the single future satellite operator for its next Direct To Home platform; the move covers Telemach, NOVA, Bulsatcom, VIVACOM, SBB and Total TV across eight countries and is expected to finish by the end of 2025 (https://united.group/united-group-and-eutelsat-develop-next-gen-dth-platform/). (bears on: programme, narrative and channels)

Ownership history. Vivacom’s ownership history is a reputation asset and a risk: Viva Ventures bought 65% of BTC for EUR 230 million in 2004, AIG bought 90% of BTC for 2.8 billion levs in 2007, Spas Roussev bought Vivacom at auction for EUR 730 million in 2015 including EUR 400 million of debt, and United Group completed its acquisition in 2020 after agreeing the deal in 2019 (https://euobserver.com/88022/bulgarias-phone-company-from-state-to-private-monopoly; https://seenews.com/news/aig-closes-acquisiion-of-90-percent-of-bulgarian-telco-btc-for-2-8-bln-levs-904186; https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/6155-bulgarian-operator-vivacom-acquired-at-auction-for-730m.html; https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/). (bears on: business and organizational context)

Acquired-customer handling. Vivacom’s customer-integration pages for Networx customers say service provision moves to Vivacom, existing prices and conditions continue during current contract terms, first Vivacom invoices would be issued after 8 March 2024, and support continues through current Networx numbers and acquired offices; this bears on customer anxiety after acquisitions (https://www.vivacom.bg/networx). (bears on: priority audiences & current state)

Regulatory context. The banked record shows a regulatory pattern: Vivacom is being treated both as a regulated infrastructure holder and as the main object of consolidation scrutiny. The banked record says CRC imposed access, non-discrimination, transparency, reference-offer and price-control duties on Vivacom for passive physical infrastructure; rivals objected to or appealed Vivacom-linked acquisitions; and the Supreme Administrative Court cleared United Group’s acquisition of Bulsatcom infrastructure assets as not notifiable under Bulgarian competition law (banked findings: CRC Decision No. 220 of 30 July 2024; A1 objection; Supreme Administrative Court Bulsatcom ruling).

Regulatory context. On 27 June 2025, the Commission on Protection of Competition, the Commission for Consumer Protection and CRC signed a cooperation agreement for consumer protection, market transparency and price-increase scrutiny before and after euro adoption. CRC said it had agreements with telecom undertakings on a working model. The consumer regulator said mobile-service prices would be included in the unified consumer portal, and that rules for consumer protection in electronic communications had already been revised with CRC. The competition authority said it was about to start a sector analysis of the telecommunications services market (https://crc.bg/en/news/1699/cpc-ccp-and-crc-join-forces-for-better-consumer-protection-and-market-transparency).

Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s amended Cybersecurity Act entered into force on 13 February 2026 and transposed NIS2, 16 months after the original deadline. Public electronic communications network providers are classed as essential entities. Regulated entities must give an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notice within 72 hours and a final report within one month. On 22 September 2025, United Group confirmed that Vivacom and Mainstream Bulgaria were affected by a malicious cyberattack; the company said some Vivacom business clients could face temporary technical difficulties, while mobile and fixed connectivity stayed operational (https://www.thefastmode.com/technology-solutions/44820-united-group-subsidiaries-vivacom-mainstream-bulgaria-hit-by-cyberattack). (bears on: constraints and guardrails)

Cloud-service incident detail. Mainstream Bulgaria said its 22 September 2025 incident began at 02:17 EET, caused temporary service disruption, triggered incident-response protocols, and led to work with independent cybersecurity experts (https://mainstream.eu/en/blog/mainstream-bulgaria-cybersecurity-incident). (bears on: constraints and guardrails)

Data-protection enforcement. On 27 March 2025, Vivacom Bulgaria EAD was fined BGN 10,000 for unlawful processing of personal data including names, address and personal identification number; the regulator required a risk assessment and technical and organizational measures to prevent similar violations (https://www.linklaters.com/en/insights/data-protected/data-protected---bulgaria). (bears on: constraints and guardrails)

Satellite infrastructure proof. Vivacom and Eutelsat launched a Bulgarian ground station in December 2023 at Vivacom’s Stara Zagora site; United Group says it is Eutelsat’s fourth European ground station and one of 35 operating globally (https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/). (bears on: programme, narrative and channels)

Satellite infrastructure proof. The Stara Zagora ground station has 18 antennas and a mini data centre linking low-Earth-orbit satellites to optical networks and data centres in Bulgaria and Europe (https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/). (bears on: programme, narrative and channels)

Satellite business standing. World Teleport Association’s 2024 rankings put Vivacom in the Independent Top 10 and in the Fast 10 for teleport operators; this independently supports the satellite-services part of Vivacom’s broader business story (https://www.worldteleport.org/?page=TopOperators; https://www.worldteleport.org/news/692727/World-Teleport-Association-Publishes-Top-Operator-Rankings-for-2024.htm). (bears on: business and organizational context)

Parent-group trading context. United Group reported Q1 2026 revenue of EUR 717.7 million, up 14% year on year, and adjusted EBITDA after leases of EUR 232.5 million, up 13%; it said growth came from subscriber growth, price increases, customer up-selling and ICT projects (https://united.group/united-group-b-v-delivers-double-digit-revenue-and-earnings-growth-in-q1-2026/). (bears on: business and organizational context)

Parent-group financing context. United Group completed a EUR 1.5 billion refinancing in January 2026, including more than EUR 1.1 billion of senior secured floating-rate notes and EUR 355 million of holding-company payment-in-kind notes, with proceeds used to refinance existing debt (https://www.paulweiss.com/insights/client-news/united-group-completes-refinancing). (bears on: business and organizational context)

pre_engagement_pack.hypothesis: Vivacom's reputation problem is that its public story does not yet turn its strongest assets into one trusted national role. The open space is a clear story about useful Bulgarian digital infrastructure, grounded in fixed internet, television, coverage, satellite capacity, public-service duties, skills programmes and local digital projects. The claim must stay inside the evidence: Vivacom can credibly support leadership in fixed internet, pay TV, coverage and satellite growth, but it cannot claim total telecom leadership across every mobile, internet or customer-experience measure. A1, Yettel, CETIN and Neterra all carry credible network, quality, infrastructure or specialist claims, so Vivacom should not compete with another broad technology claim. It should prove the national outcomes that only its mix of incumbent infrastructure, United Group scale, EON, Bulsatcom, satellite assets, public-sector work and skills programmes can connect. (rests on: The white space)(rests on: Vivacom self-claim verdict)(rests on: The narratives running about it)(rests on: Category context)(rests on: Each peer's narrative)

hypothesis_test.confirms: The hypothesis holds if client data and stakeholder interviews show that decision-makers, employees, public-sector customers, and media accept Vivacom's infrastructure scale as useful national progress when it is tied to named outcomes rather than broad leadership language.
hypothesis_test.overturns: The hypothesis fails if audience research shows that Vivacom's scale mainly triggers former-incumbent, market-power, pricing, or service-friction associations that cannot be offset by fixed internet, television, satellite, public-sector, and skills proof.

style_note.self_reference: Vivacom refers to itself by the brand name, by the company name, and through first-person plural forms in Bulgarian when it wants a warmer social or employer tone.

record.question: Vivacom now has fixed, mobile, television, satellite, smart-city, cloud, and digital-education proof in the public record; which of these businesses must sit at the centre of the corporate story, and which should stay as supporting proof?
record.finding:
What the company does. Vivacom is a Bulgarian telecommunications provider serving households, businesses, and institutions (https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
What the company does. Vivacom offers mobile voice, fixed voice, mobile broadband, fixed broadband, interactive TV, satellite TV, Internet of Things, smart-city, digital education, and cloud services (https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
What the company does. Vivacom says it provides telecommunications solutions for private and business clients, including mobile and fixed voice, high-speed optical internet, satellite TV, interactive TV, and tailored offers for corporate clients (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
What the company does. United Group describes Vivacom as a leading provider of mobile, fixed broadband, and television services in Bulgaria (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
What the company does. United Group said in 2020 that Vivacom was the first telecommunications company in Bulgaria and supplied fibre broadband, mobile communications, and digital TV to private and commercial customers (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/).
What the company does. Vivacom says its own infrastructure includes mobile, fixed, terrestrial, copper, and satellite assets (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
What the company does. Vivacom says its 5G network covers 92% of Bulgaria’s population, its 4G LTE network covers 99.95%, and its 2G and 3G networks cover 99.99% (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
What the company does. Vivacom says its fixed network covers 1.6 million homes and includes the first and only 10 GIGA network in Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
What the company does. Vivacom says it has more than 200 own retail stores across Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
What the company does. SeeNews says Vivacom provides professional internet and data services, radio and television data transfer, leased lines, VoIP, and public payphones, in addition to fixed-line telephony, mobile communications, internet, and digital TV (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
What the company does. Vivacom’s 2018 Annual Activities Report says Vivacom develops, operates, and maintains national fixed and mobile networks and a data system for Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf). The same report says Vivacom owned Plana teleport, serving orbital positions in Europe, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf).
What the company does. Vivacom’s 2018 Annual Activities Report says NURTS Group was a Vivacom-owned provider of radio and television broadcasting, terrestrial and satellite signal transmission, and colocation services in Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf). The same report says NURTS Group owned and operated more than 500 radio and television stations across Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf).
What the company does. SeeNews says Vivacom owned and operated the Plana Teleport satellite facility with 40 antennae at the end of 2016 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
What the company does. CRC lists Vivacom Bulgaria EAD with nationwide radio-frequency assignments in the 700 MHz, 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 2 GHz, 2.6 GHz, 3.6 GHz, and 26 GHz bands (https://crc.bg/en/articles/2535/allocation-of-radio-frequency-spectrum-in-700-mhz-800-mhz-900-mhz-1800-mhz-2-ghz-2-6-ghz-3-6-ghz-and-26-ghz-bands).
What the company does. CRC lists Vivacom's 700 MHz and 800 MHz licences as expiring on 28 November 2038, its 900 MHz and 1800 MHz licences as expiring on 7 June 2034, its 2 GHz licence as expiring on 25 April 2035, its 2.6 GHz licence as expiring on 1 March 2041, its 3.6 GHz licence as expiring on 11 May 2041, and its 26 GHz assignments as expiring on 17 November 2042 and 24 November 2042 (https://crc.bg/en/articles/2535/allocation-of-radio-frequency-spectrum-in-700-mhz-800-mhz-900-mhz-1800-mhz-2-ghz-2-6-ghz-3-6-ghz-and-26-ghz-bands).
What the company does. Vivacom also offers online insurance intermediation through an insurance site powered by Boleron; the Financial Supervision Commission register confirms Vivacom Bulgaria EAD is listed as an insurance broker (https://insurance.vivacom.bg/grazhdanska-otgovornost-online/; https://www.fsc.bg/zastrahovatelna-deynost/spisaczi-podnadzorni-licza/zastrahovatelni-brokeri/).
What the company does. Vivacom says it holds CRC permit No. 1610 for satellite broadcasting (https://www.vivacom.bg/business/satelitni-uslugi).
What the company does. Vivacom says Plana Teleport occupies 60,000 square metres and has more than 70 antennas across L, S, C, X, Ku, DBS, and Ka bands, with 24x7 control and support (https://www.vivacom.bg/business/satelitni-uslugi).
What the company does. Vivacom says Plana Teleport can work with satellites from 40 degrees West to 90 degrees East (https://www.vivacom.bg/business/satelitni-uslugi).
What the company does. United Group says Vivacom’s satellite portfolio is supported by three ground stations in Bulgaria and two more facilities under development for low Earth orbit connectivity projects (https://united.group/updates-from-our-greek-and-bulgarian-operations/).
What the company does. United Group says Vivacom broadcasts more than 600 TV channels and provides connectivity across Europe, Africa, South America, Asia, and Antarctica (https://united.group/vivacom-satellite-global-growth/).
