findings: Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Investors and owners matter because Vivacom is a subsidiary inside United Group. United Group is majority owned by BC Partners and has owned Vivacom since the 2020 closing. United Group says it is active in eight countries, has nearly 16 million users and 15,000 employees, and generated more than EUR 2.7 billion in annual revenue in its 2024 Bulsatcom announcement. (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Owner relations matter because Vivacom sits under a parent with public governance conflict. Economic.bg reported in August 2025 that United Group had a control dispute between founder Dragan Sholak and majority shareholder BC Partners. It reported that Sholak filed a lawsuit after his removal and a dispute over EUR 200 million in bonuses. It also reported market speculation about a possible United Group sale at EUR 8 billion. (https://www.economic.bg/en/a/view/top-management-reshuffle-at-vivacom-director-leaves-spas-rusev-returns)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Communications Regulation Commission matters because it is the national sector regulator and source of market baselines. CRC said Bulgaria's electronic communications market was BGN 4.021 billion in 2024, up 5.7% from 2023. CRC said A1, Vivacom and Yettel formed 97.8% of fixed voice subscribers and 94.0% of fixed voice retail revenue. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. CRC matters for Vivacom's market standing. CRC said Vivacom was the fixed internet leader in 2024 with 39.4% of subscribers and 37.1% of revenue. CRC said Vivacom was the pay TV leader in 2024 with 59.6% of subscribers and 56.5% of revenue after Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria were incorporated into Vivacom. CRC said Vivacom became second in mobile voice revenue in 2024 and its mobile voice revenue share rose from 25.4% in 2020 to 32.0% in 2024. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. CRC matters for public-interest duties. CRC said Vivacom continued to provide public payphones at main entry points and high-traffic places such as airports, ports, railway and bus stations, motorways, hospitals and police stations. CRC said Vivacom continued free calls to emergency numbers from all public payphones. CRC said Vivacom continued tariff packages for low-income users, people with disabilities and people with special social needs. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Commission for Protection of Competition matters because Vivacom's acquisitions have been contested. PPF Telecom Group said CPC approved transactions linked to Networx and Telnet despite court hearings and a court-ordered review. NERA said CPC cleared Vivacom's acquisition of Telnet and Networx unconditionally at Phase 2 on 29 June 2023. (https://www.ppf.eu/en/press-release/ppf-telecom-group-dismayed-by-regulatory-ruling-taken-in-bulgaria; https://www.nera.com/experience/2023/bulgarian-telco-vivacom-cleared-to-acquire-telnet-and-networx-.html)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The European Commission matters for ownership control because United Group said the Vivacom acquisition followed European Commission approval in April 2020. It also matters for earlier history because Vivacom's own history says the 2012 restructuring received approval from the European Commission and other authorities. (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Employees matter because the current strategy follows a management change. SeeNews reported that Asen Velikov replaced Nikolai Andreev as Vivacom CEO in August 2025. SeeNews also reported Stan Miller became supervisory board chair and Spas Rusev and Stan Miller joined the board, replacing Viktoriya Boklag and Yanez Zhivko. Vivacom's own management page lists Asen Velikov as CEO, Ognyan Toshmakov as CFO from 13 July 2026, Ivo Zlatev as chief legal officer, and Malina Chavdarova as head of human capital management. (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-vivacom-names-ceo-1279653; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Media matter both as channels and as parent-group context. United Group owns Vivacom in Bulgaria and also owns Nova Broadcasting Group in Bulgaria. Economic.bg reported that point when discussing Vivacom's management change and United Group's parent conflict. (https://www.economic.bg/en/a/view/top-management-reshuffle-at-vivacom-director-leaves-spas-rusev-returns)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Communities and civic organisations matter because Vivacom frames public contribution around education, environment and local projects. Vivacom says its Regional Grant supports civic organisations across Bulgaria on education and environmental protection. Vivacom says it has supported 128 projects by 115 civic organisations with more than BGN 700,000. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/sotsialna-otgovornost)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Students, schools, STEM communities and local authorities matter because Vivacom names them in its social and business activity. Vivacom says Job Lab targets pupils in grades 11 and 12. Vivacom says it supports Bulgarian science olympiad teams. Vivacom says it creates smart-city and digital-modernisation options for more than 130 Bulgarian municipalities. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/sotsialna-otgovornost; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Business customers and public-sector customers matter because Vivacom says it offers individual proposals for corporate clients and develops services in the Internet of Things and smart cities. The supplied brief also names business and enterprise customers, partners, regulators, government stakeholders, media, talent, the public, consumers and parent-group stakeholders as audiences to prioritise. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md)

Who is talking. Vivacom talks through its corporate site, its management page, its social responsibility page and its sustainability page. Its current listed CEO is Asen Velikov, who joined Vivacom in 1999, became CFO in 2013, joined the management board in 2014, and is now member of the management board and CEO. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip)

Who is talking. United Group talks often about Vivacom as owner and parent. It announced the Vivacom acquisition in 2019, welcomed Vivacom into the group in 2020, announced the Bulsatcom completion in 2024, and published a July 2026 item backing Vivacom's fibre, 5G and television growth. (https://united.group/united-group-acquires-vivacom/; https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom; https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/)

Who is talking. Bulgarian regulators talk about Vivacom in annual market data and merger decisions. CRC names A1, Vivacom and Yettel as Bulgaria's three mobile voice providers in 2024. CRC also records Vivacom's fixed voice, fixed internet, pay TV, universal service and emergency-call duties. (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf)

Who is talking. Competitors and their owners talk about Vivacom in competition terms. PPF Telecom Group and Yettel Bulgaria criticised CPC decisions on Vivacom transactions in July 2023. Vivacom answered through a public denial carried by Broadband TV News. (https://www.ppf.eu/en/press-release/ppf-telecom-group-dismayed-by-regulatory-ruling-taken-in-bulgaria; https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2023/07/04/vivacom-dismisses-unfounded-concerns-from-competitors/)

Who is talking. Business and sector media are active voices on Vivacom. SeeNews reported the August 2025 CEO change to Asen Velikov and the reshuffled supervisory board. Economic.bg linked the same reshuffle to United Group owner tensions and the return of former owner Spas Rusev to the board. Broadband TV News covered Vivacom's competition disputes and acquisitions. (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-vivacom-names-ceo-1279653; https://www.economic.bg/en/a/view/top-management-reshuffle-at-vivacom-director-leaves-spas-rusev-returns; https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2023/07/04/vivacom-dismisses-unfounded-concerns-from-competitors/)

Who is talking. Technology partners talk about Vivacom's network and platform choices. Nokia announced a 2020 multi-year Vivacom fibre deal covering GPON and XGS-PON and more than 1.5 million households in major cities. Eutelsat and Vivacom announced a fourth European ground station in Bulgaria in 2023. (https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-helps-vivacom-bulgaria-deploy-next-generation-fiber-network/; https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/)

Advocates and critics. United Group is a clear advocate for Vivacom's investment story. In July 2026, United Group said Vivacom's priority areas were fibre, 5G and television, and its CEO Stan Miller said the group would keep backing the Bulgarian team. (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/)

Advocates and critics. Vivacom's own management is an advocate for market consolidation. In July 2023, Vivacom rejected A1 and Yettel allegations as unfounded and said Bulgaria's fixed broadband and pay-TV markets remained multi-player markets. It said Vivacom held 31% of fixed broadband and 33% of pay TV by subscribers. (https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2023/07/04/vivacom-dismisses-unfounded-concerns-from-competitors/)

Advocates and critics. PPF Telecom Group and Yettel Bulgaria are open critics of Vivacom's acquisition path. In July 2023, PPF said CPC approvals would put Vivacom near 70% of internet access in Rousse and near 50% in Varna, Razgrad, Silistra and Sofia City. PPF also said Vivacom held 32.9% of television distribution and 31.4% of fixed internet nationally before the Bulsatcom infrastructure question. (https://www.ppf.eu/en/press-release/ppf-telecom-group-dismayed-by-regulatory-ruling-taken-in-bulgaria)

Advocates and critics. A1 Bulgaria is a critic in the same competition dispute. Broadband TV News reported that Vivacom rejected allegations made by A1 and Yettel after CPC cleared Vivacom's acquisition of Networx and Telnet. (https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2023/07/04/vivacom-dismisses-unfounded-concerns-from-competitors/)

Advocates and critics. The mayor of Stara Zagora was an advocate for Vivacom's satellite project with Eutelsat. United Group quoted Mayor Zhivko Todorov saying the project would stimulate the city and support digital inclusion across Eurasia. (https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/)

Client self-description and verdict. Vivacom says: "Vivacom е иноватор, който вече 15 години движи развитието на телеком сектора в страната." It also says it has invested nearly BGN 3 billion and serves more than 2 million customers using more than 5.5 million services. CRC corroborates Vivacom's strong market position in fixed internet, pay TV and mobile voice, but it does not use the same brand wording. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf) (bears on: business and organizational context)

Company history and former names. Vivacom traces its history to the first Bulgarian communications body created in Pleven in 1879. Vivacom says it is the successor to BTC, Bulgaria's first telecommunications company. In 2004, the state sold 65% of BTC to Viva Ventures, a unit of Advent International; SeeNews records the price as EUR 275.356 million, while Novinite records a widely cited EUR 230 million sale figure. BTC Mobile launched services under the vivatel brand in November 2005. BTC and vivatel combined under the Vivacom brand in 2009. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525; https://www.novinite.com/articles/139418/Bulgaria%2BDefeated%2Bin%2BCourt%2Bby%2BViva%2BVentures%2Bover%2BTelco%2BDeal) (bears on: business and organizational context)

Ownership changes and reported prices. AIG Global Investment Group agreed in 2007 to buy Viva Ventures' 65% BTC stake for EUR 1.08 billion and expected to secure a further 25% stake. Creditor banks were reported in 2012 to have agreed to sell a majority stake in Vivacom for EUR 130 million while debt would be cut to EUR 588 million. VTB Capital secured a majority stake in 2015 for EUR 130 million. United Group agreed in 2019 to acquire Vivacom for a reported EUR 1.2 billion, and the deal closed in 2020. (https://www.rttnews.com/294831/aig-global-investment-group-to-buy-viva-ventures-65-stake-in-bulgarian-telecommunications-for-eur-1-08-bln-update.aspx; https://www.fierce-network.com/europe/banks-agree-to-buy-bulgaria-s-vivacom; https://www.globalprivatecapital.org/newsroom/vtb-capital-to-exit-vivacom-to-bc-partners-backed-united-group-in-usd1-3-billion-acquisition/; https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/) (bears on: decision-maker & approval path)

Community and civic programmes. Vivacom says it has donated more than BGN 6 million to more than 300 causes and more than 200 organisations over 15 years. It says its Regional Grant has backed 128 projects by 115 civic organisations with more than BGN 700,000. It says Job Lab targets 11th and 12th grade pupils in Sofia, Blagoevgrad, Varna and Veliko Tarnovo. It says it donated nearly BGN 140,000 to science olympiad teams and BGN 10,000 plus unlimited internet for the 2024 International Olympiad in AI in Burgas. Independent sources in this pass did not verify each grant count. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/sotsialna-otgovornost; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata) (bears on: priority audiences & current state)

ESG claims and proof needs. Vivacom says it follows United Group sustainability targets. These include net zero across the value chain by 2040, a 90% cut in scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 from a 2020 base year, 100% active annual renewable electricity sourcing by 2027, 40% women in management by 2030, 40 training hours per employee each year by 2030, and annual ethics training for all employees. Independent sources in this pass did not verify progress against each target. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ustojchivo-razvitie) (bears on: constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Network claims and proof status. Vivacom says its 5G network covers 92% of Bulgaria's population and that it was the first operator to launch commercial 5G in all 27 district cities in September 2020. It says it has the fastest fibre network for home internet and 1.6 million homes in fibre coverage. CRC's 2024 report corroborates Vivacom's fixed internet lead by subscribers and revenue, but this pass did not find CRC verification of the 92% 5G claim. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf) (bears on: reputation problem / desired perception)

Cybersecurity incident. United Group reported that Vivacom and Mainstream Bulgaria were hit by a cyberattack on 22 September 2025. United Group said core mobile and fixed connectivity remained working. United Group said relevant authorities and regulators were notified. (https://www.thefastmode.com/technology-solutions/44820-united-group-subsidiaries-vivacom-mainstream-bulgaria-hit-by-cyberattack) (bears on: constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The banked record shows Vivacom’s stakeholder map is not only a customer and competitor map. It puts United Group and BC Partners above Vivacom, CRC and CPC around market conduct, the European Commission around ownership control, employees around the management change, media around both Vivacom and Nova Broadcasting Group, and civic organisations, schools and municipalities around social and local projects. (banked findings: owners and investors; CRC; CPC; European Commission; employees; media; communities; students; business and public-sector customers)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The banked record shows ownership history is a live stakeholder issue, not background. Vivacom moved from state ownership to Viva Ventures, then AIG, then creditor and VTB-linked control, then United Group, with reported values ranging from EUR 130 million in restructuring-era sales to about EUR 1.2 billion in the United Group deal. The same record now links Vivacom to a 2025 United Group control dispute and reported EUR 8 billion sale speculation. (banked findings: company history and former names; ownership changes and reported prices; owner relations)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Courts now matter alongside competition regulators. SeeNews reported on 19 February 2026 that Bulgaria’s Supreme Administrative Court issued a final ruling clearing United Group’s Bulsatcom infrastructure-assets acquisition after appeals by A1 Bulgaria, Yettel Bulgaria and Cetin Bulgaria. The court said the assessed deals did not form a notifiable concentration. (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Commission for Personal Data Protection matters for reputation and legal guardrails. Linklaters reported that Vivacom Bulgaria EAD was fined BGN 10,000 on 27 March 2025 for unlawful processing of personal data including names, addresses and personal identification numbers. Linklaters said the Commission required Vivacom to conduct a risk assessment and implement technical and work-process measures to prevent similar violations. (https://www.linklaters.com/en/insights/data-protected/data-protected---bulgaria)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Communications Regulation Commission matters for service-reliability pressure, not only market shares. Telecompaper reported that CRC requested Vivacom to conduct an internal investigation into a 25 April 2025 network and services incident. Telecompaper reported that CRC expected Vivacom to identify the causes, present risk-reduction measures and report results within seven days. (https://www.telecompaper.com/news/bulgarian-regulator-orders-vivacom-to-investigate-cause-of-network-failure--1535070)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Consumer Protection Commission matters for contract and pricing conduct. BNR reported that, from 2025, users may cancel mobile-service contracts without fees within 30 days when an operator announces inflation indexation. BNR said this followed meetings between the commission and telecom companies and an agreement regulating fee-free termination. (https://bnrnews.bg/en/post/104442/citizens-to-be-able-to-cancel-contracts-for-mobile-services-without-fees-from-2025)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Civil society organisations remain a live stakeholder set around Vivacom’s social contribution. BAIT reported that the ninth Vivacom Regional Grant awarded BGN 100,000 to 10 civil society organisations in 2024, with BGN 10,000 for each finalist. BAIT reported a record 395 applications from 361 organisations. (https://www.bait.bg/en/novini/vivacom-regional-grant-supports-10-projects-with-bgn-100-000/)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. The Bulgarian Center for Not-for-Profit Law is more than a passive beneficiary in Vivacom’s local giving. BAIT quoted BCNL saying it had partnered with Vivacom since the start of the Regional Grant and that the ninth edition added an accelerator lab for finalists. (https://www.bait.bg/en/novini/vivacom-regional-grant-supports-10-projects-with-bgn-100-000/)

Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations. Employees and future talent matter because Vivacom also talks to students as a workforce pipeline. United Group’s LinkedIn post said Vivacom’s Job Lab pilot would run from February to May 2026 in Sofia, Blagoevgrad, Varna and Veliko Tarnovo and include school workshops, independent student work, skills assessment, a Vivacom HQ visit and an AI and digital-skills module. (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/united-group-b.v._joblab-unitedgroup-vivacom-activity-7425125424449511424-1jtJ)

Who is talking. The Consumer Protection Commission is talking about mobile operators as a consumer-rights issue. BNR reported in 2025 that chair Maria Filipova ordered operators to stop unilateral contract changes without consumer consent and said fines could reach BGN 50,000 for each unfair commercial practice. BNR said two mobile operators had changed existing contract terms, including monthly charges, without written agreement from consumers. (https://bnrnews.bg/en/post/123374/cpc-issues-an-order-prohibiting-the-unilateral-price-increases-by-mobile-operators)

Who is talking. The Ombudsman Institution is talking about mobile operators as a citizen-harm issue. Its Secretary General said on 11 March 2025 that the institution had opposed controversial price increases for years and had acted after complaints from citizens. The same source named Yettel, Vivacom and A1 in the price-indexation sequence. (https://www.ombudsman.bg/en/n/ombudsmans-secretary-general-ombudsman-institution-sounds-years-long-alarm-a-2293)

Who is talking. Sector and legal media are talking about Vivacom through court and regulator decisions. SeeNews reported the final Supreme Administrative Court ruling on Bulsatcom in February 2026. BNR reported Consumer Protection Commission action on unilateral price changes in 2025. Telecompaper reported that CRC ordered Vivacom to investigate an April 2025 network failure. (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035; https://bnrnews.bg/en/post/123374/cpc-issues-an-order-prohibiting-the-unilateral-price-increases-by-mobile-operators; https://www.telecompaper.com/news/bulgarian-regulator-orders-vivacom-to-investigate-cause-of-network-failure--1535070)

Who is talking. Technology and platform partners are talking about Vivacom’s operating base. Netcracker talked about a 2026 Vivacom IT modernisation extension. United Cloud talked about EON’s origin, features and regional use. United Group talked about Vivacom’s EON, fibre, 5G and television growth. (https://www.netcracker.com/news/press-releases/netcracker-and-vivacom-extend-long-term-partnership-for-innovative-it-modernization-program; https://united.cloud/latest/eon-tv-and-chill; https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/)

Advocates and critics. The banked record shows a three-sided argument around consolidation. United Group and Vivacom frame acquisitions as investment and service improvement. CRC, CPC, courts and the European Commission frame them as matters for approval, market definition and public-interest duties. PPF, Yettel and A1 frame them as concentration risk. (banked findings: United Group owner findings; CRC market-standing findings; CPC acquisition findings; PPF/Yettel/A1 critic findings; Vivacom denial finding)

Advocates and critics. A1 Group criticised Vivacom-linked acquisition activity in 2023 and said Vivacom could acquire over 60% of the TV distribution market and nearly 40% of the internet market. A1 Group said it had alerted the European Commission about concerns over what it called the hidden buyout of Bulsatcom by United Group. (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594)

Advocates and critics. The Supreme Administrative Court gave United Group a clear legal win on 19 February 2026. SeeNews reported that the court finally cleared the Bulsatcom infrastructure-assets acquisition after appeals by A1 Bulgaria, Yettel Bulgaria and Cetin Bulgaria. The court said the network deal and base-station infrastructure-assets deal did not form a notifiable concentration under Bulgarian competition law. (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035)

Advocates and critics. Customers are visible critics in public review space. Trustpilot listed Vivacom with a 1.3 score from 203 reviews, 41 reviews in the previous 12 months and 92% one-star reviews. Trustpilot also marked the profile as unclaimed and warned that Vivacom had not invited customers, so the reviews may not be representative. (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.vivacom.bg)

Advocates and critics. The Ombudsman Institution criticised mobile-service price increases and named Vivacom as one of the operators that followed Yettel’s end-2022 indexation move. It said public discontent produced numerous complaints and that the Ombudsman referred issues to the Commission for Consumer Protection, the Communications Regulation Commission and other authorities. (https://www.ombudsman.bg/en/n/ombudsmans-secretary-general-ombudsman-institution-sounds-years-long-alarm-a-2293)

EON platform origin and proof status. United Group says Vivacom has backed IPTV growth through EON, which it calls an award-winning TV platform developed by United Cloud. United Cloud says EON emerged in 2017 and was used on more than 1.5 million devices across eight markets by the end of 2021. No independent source in this pass judged the award claim. (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgarias-telecoms-market-expands/; https://united.cloud/latest/eon-tv-and-chill) (bears on: programme, narrative and channels)

Billing and customer-platform partner. Netcracker said on 11 February 2026 that Vivacom extended a long-term IT partnership and would upgrade Netcracker Revenue Management for postpaid mobile and fixed lines serving B2C and B2B customers. Netcracker quoted Asen Velikov saying the platform would support “rapid growth”. This is partner evidence, not independent market proof. (https://www.netcracker.com/news/press-releases/netcracker-and-vivacom-extend-long-term-partnership-for-innovative-it-modernization-program) (bears on: business and organizational context)

Satellite-services standing. United Group said on 20 February 2025 that Vivacom entered the World Teleport Association Independent Top 10 for the first time and ranked among the top five global operators for satellite-services revenue growth in the 2024 report. United Group said Vivacom operates Plana Earth Station and Mogila Ground Station, has two more ground stations under construction, broadcasts more than 600 TV channels and provides connectivity across Europe, Africa, South America, Asia and Antarctica. The World Teleport Association page was not accessible in this pass, so the ranking remains a United Group-reported independent ranking. (https://united.group/vivacom-satellite-global-growth/) (bears on: reputation problem / desired perception)

Parent-group energy proof. United Group said it is investing EUR 120 million in Bulgarian renewable-energy projects, including 52 MWp of solar power and 72 MW of wind power. SeeNews reported that the projects are planned to generate 310,000 MWh annually by 2027 and reduce CO2 emissions by 120,000 tonnes per year. findings: Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s telecom sector is governed by EU rules including the European Electronic Communications Code, ePrivacy Directive, Net Neutrality Regulation, Roaming Regulation, Gigabit Infrastructure Act and EU termination-rate rules; Bulgarian core laws include the Electronic Communications Act and Electronic Communications Networks and Physical Infrastructure Act (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. Telecom and adjacent digital activity in Bulgaria is also affected by the General Data Protection Regulation, Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Cybersecurity Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, NIS2 Directive and Critical Entity Resilience Directive; this confirms the supplied brief’s legal and AI-policy constraints (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. The Communications Regulation Commission is the independent telecom regulator; the Ministry of Transport and Communications and Ministry of e-Government set ICT, digital administration and cybersecurity policy; the National Radio Frequency Spectrum Council handles national spectrum-planning proposals (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

Regulatory context. CRC Decision No. 220 of 30 July 2024 found no effective competition in wholesale access to passive physical infrastructure, named Vivacom as having significant individual impact, and imposed access, non-discrimination, transparency, reference-offer and price-control duties (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC launched a fourth-round analysis of local access at a fixed location, and by Decision No. 251 of 29 August 2025 ordered extra information on fixed access via mobile network for 2021-2023; this keeps fixed access and 5G-based home internet inside active review (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC says Vivacom met all universal-service quality target values in 2024, did not request unfair-burden compensation by the 30 June 2024 statutory deadline, and had a 46% drop in universal-service complaints versus the prior period (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CRC says 2024 universal-service complaints to Vivacom were mainly technical failures at 27% of complaints; termination complaints rose to 16% from 2% in 2023, and the other category rose 18 percentage points to 29% (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Regulatory context. CMS says CRC awarded 20-year 3.6 GHz licences to A1, Vivacom and Yettel in April 2021, and assigned 700 MHz and 800 MHz bands to the same three operators in December 2023 for 15 years; CMS says total licence payments were about BGN 13.4 million (https://cms.law/en/int/expert-guides/cms-expert-guide-to-5g-regulation-and-law/bulgaria).

Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s Supreme Administrative Court issued a final ruling in February 2026 clearing United Group’s acquisition of Bulsatcom telecom infrastructure assets after appeals by A1 Bulgaria, Yettel Bulgaria and Cetin Bulgaria; the court said the deal and base-station infrastructure asset deal were not a notifiable concentration under Bulgarian competition law (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-supreme-court-clears-united-groups-acquisition-of-bulsatcom-1290035).

Regulatory context. A1 Group publicly objected in July 2023 to CPC approval of Vivacom acquisitions of Networx-Bulgaria and six smaller operators, saying the deals could give Vivacom more than 60% of TV distribution and nearly 40% of internet; CRC’s 2024 market data later reported Vivacom at 59.6% of pay-TV subscribers and 39.4% of fixed internet subscribers (https://newsroom.a1.com/news-a1-group-deeply-unsettled-by-an-unexpected-decision-of-the-bulgarian-commission-on-protection-of-competition?id=182022&l=english&menueid=14594; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

ESG context. United Group says its 2024 sustainability results included 61% electricity from renewable sources, a 52% cut in Scope 1 and 2 emissions against its 2020 baseline, a 13% improvement in its Network Efficiency Index, 25% refurbished customer premises equipment among installed devices, more than 2,300 kg of e-waste recovered, and more than 1,500 smartphones recovered through customer take-back programs (https://united.group/united-group-releases-2024-sustainability-report-highlighting-tangible-progress-across-esg-priorities/).

ESG context. United Group says it is building three solar plants and one wind farm in Bulgaria; by 2027 these assets are planned to supply 160% of electricity needed for the Group’s Bulgarian operations, cover 65% of total Group electricity use, remove about 120,000 tonnes of CO2 from Bulgaria’s grid each year, reach 124 MW combined capacity, and produce 310,000 MWh a year (https://united.group/united-group-enters-renewable-energy-production/).

ESG context. Regulatory context. Bulgaria’s amended Cybersecurity Act entered into force on 13 February 2026 and transposed NIS2, 16 months after the original deadline. Public electronic communications network providers are classed as essential entities. Regulated entities must give an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notice within 72 hours and a final report within one month. Essential-entity penalties can reach EUR 10 million or 2% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, with manager liability also introduced (https://www.schoenherr.eu/content/bulgaria-implements-nis-2-directive-key-changes-to-the-cybersecurity-act).

Vivacom and Eutelsat launched a Bulgarian ground station in December 2023 at Vivacom’s Stara Zagora site; United Group says it is Eutelsat’s fourth European ground station and one of 35 operating globally (https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/). The Stara Zagora ground station has 18 antennas and a mini data centre linking low-Earth-orbit satellites to optical networks and data centres in Bulgaria and Europe (https://united.group/vivacom-and-eutelsat-group-are-launching-in-bulgaria-the-fourth-european-ground-station/). draft.hypothesis: Vivacom's reputation problem is that its public story does not yet turn its strongest assets into one trusted national role. The open space is a clear story about useful Bulgarian digital infrastructure, grounded in fixed internet, television, coverage, satellite capacity, public-service duties, skills programmes and local digital projects. The claim must stay inside the evidence: Vivacom can credibly support leadership in fixed internet, pay TV, coverage and satellite growth, but it cannot claim total telecom leadership across every mobile, internet or customer-experience measure. A1, Yettel, CETIN and Neterra all carry credible network, quality, infrastructure or specialist claims, so Vivacom should not compete with another broad technology claim. It should prove the national outcomes that only its mix of incumbent infrastructure, United Group scale, EON, Bulsatcom, satellite assets, public-sector work and skills programmes can connect. (rests on: The white space)(rests on: Vivacom self-claim verdict)(rests on: The narratives running about it)(rests on: Category context)(rests on: Each peer's narrative)

hypothesis_test.confirms: The hypothesis holds if client data and stakeholder interviews show that decision-makers, employees, public-sector customers, and media accept Vivacom's infrastructure scale as useful national progress when it is tied to named outcomes rather than broad leadership language.
hypothesis_test.overturns: The hypothesis fails if audience research shows that Vivacom's scale mainly triggers former-incumbent, market-power, pricing, or service-friction associations that cannot be offset by fixed internet, television, satellite, public-sector, and skills proof.

style_note.tone: Vivacom's own voice is direct, service-led, and confident. It often opens with the customer benefit, then supports it with network scale, product detail, or programme proof.
style_note.sentence_length: The client uses mostly short to medium sentences in public-facing copy, with longer sentences when it lists service features, coverage figures, or programme details.
style_note.vocabulary: The client's vocabulary centres on connectivity, customers, digital services, innovation, technology, coverage, speed, education, skills, entertainment, support, and Bulgaria's digital development.
style_note.self_reference: Vivacom refers to itself by the brand name, by the company name, and through first-person plural forms in Bulgarian when it wants a warmer social or employer tone.

questions.question: Vivacom now has fixed, mobile, television, satellite, smart-city, cloud, and digital-education proof in the public record; which of these businesses must sit at the centre of the corporate story, and which should stay as supporting proof? (builds on: What the company does)

The public record shows strong fixed internet and pay-TV positions, Bulsatcom integration, and United Group backing, but it does not give a current Vivacom-only revenue split by consumer, enterprise, public sector, mobile, broadband, television, and information and communications technology services; what internal split can we use to keep the strategy tied to the business model? (builds on: Its business model)

Asen Velikov became the public chief executive officer after the 2025 leadership change, and a new chief financial officer was named in July 2026; what leadership story should the corporate platform help the new team tell in its first year? (builds on: Its leadership)

Pikasa counted 198 Vivacom media articles in Q1 2026, but described much of that volume as public-relations announcements with weak audience response; what would make earned coverage count as reputation progress rather than output volume? (builds on: How much media coverage it gets)
questions.builds_on: How much media coverage it gets

questions.question: The record shows positive proof in coverage, fixed internet, satellite, and employer signals, but customer reviews, outages, data-protection cases, consumer-law rulings, and competition concerns pull the other way; which risk line must the strategy address openly? (builds on: The sentiment of that coverage)

Vivacom's strongest defensible story is infrastructure scale, while that same scale feeds former-incumbent and market-power concern; how far can we lean into scale before it starts to hurt the desired perception? (builds on: The narratives running about it)

Vivacom's digital presence spans My Vivacom, EON, Vivacom Support on Viber, Pay by Vivacom, Happy Call, GAME ON, and social channels; which digital services should prove the corporate story, and which are mainly sales or service channels? (builds on: Channels)
Pikasa found Vivacom strongest on Instagram but weak at turning YouTube reach into response; what audience behaviour should the new corporate platform change on each channel? (builds on: Presence)

Vivacom's public tone moves from formal scale claims on corporate pages to warmer first-person plural language on LinkedIn and youth programmes; which version feels most like the voice the company wants in corporate reputation work? (builds on: Tone of voice)

The peer map shows A1 and Yettel as national retail rivals, Neterra as an enterprise and infrastructure specialist, and CETIN as a wholesale network-infrastructure peer; which competitor set should the corporate platform be built to beat? (builds on: Three to five peers)

A1 can claim breadth and speed, Yettel can claim certified mobile quality and employer trust, Vivacom can claim fixed internet, pay TV, coverage, and satellite proof, and Neterra can claim specialist infrastructure; which leadership claims are worth making, and which should we avoid? (builds on: The white space)

A1 and Yettel have both challenged Vivacom-linked consolidation, while the Supreme Administrative Court cleared the Bulsatcom infrastructure-assets transaction; how should the corporate story handle market-power scrutiny without repeating competitor framing? (builds on: Competition clearance development)

The stakeholder map includes United Group and BC Partners, the Communications Regulation Commission, competition and consumer authorities, employees, media, municipalities, schools, public-sector customers, business customers, and civic organisations; which groups must approve, which must believe, and which must only not object? (builds on: Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations)
questions.builds_on: Who matters -- investors, regulators, employees, media, communities and non-governmental organisations

questions.question: United Group, regulators, competitors, customers, app-store users, and sector media all talk about Vivacom in different ways; whose voice most shapes the reputation problem today? (builds on: Who is talking)

Customers and public authorities criticise pricing, contracts, outages, and data handling, while United Group, partners, and network testers support the investment and infrastructure story; where must the new narrative carry a proof point rather than a promise? (builds on: Advocates and critics)

Vivacom faces telecom, competition, consumer, data, cyber, Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act scrutiny; which claim areas need mandatory Legal and Regulatory review before any client-facing use? (builds on: Regulatory context)

business_outcome.outcome: Support growth through preference and value in a mature telecom market by rebuilding corporate reputation, leadership trust, employer appeal, and a differentiated role beyond core connectivity.

must_say: Show a genuine role in the country's digital progress.
Build one company story rather than disconnected activity claims.
must_avoid: Do not fall back into state-utility or former-monopoly framing.
Do not recycle shared category claims around technology leadership, environmental, social and governance performance, or employer branding as the central idea.
Do not use competitive price-war messaging as corporate positioning.
Do not introduce political framing.

expected_outputs: Evidence base and readiness check.
Two to three reasoned positioning territories with a recommended direction and rationale.
Corporate brand platform and message architecture.
Pillar architecture derived from evidence.
Stakeholder and executive thought-leadership map.
Twelve-month roadmap or campaign platform linked to business moments.
Measurement framework aligned to AMEC Barcelona Principles 4.0 and the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework.
success_criteria: The work surfaces gaps before writing.
The work flags that positioning is undecided.
Pillars and positioning are reasoned from evidence.
Every recommendation traces to input and separates fact from judgment.
The work presents options for client decision rather than asserting a finished answer.
The first message architecture is small enough for a client decision meeting and substantive enough to test the central strategic bet.

do_not_say: Do not say Vivacom is the telecom leader without naming the metric.
Do not say Vivacom is the best mobile network when independent sources split speed, reliability, and coverage across operators.
Do not say Vivacom is an innovator unless the claim is tied to a named proof point.
Do not claim environmental, social and governance leadership without group-verified or Vivacom-specific proof.
Do not invent clients, revenue splits, market shares, campaign results, budget, timeline, or approval status.
Do not present prior agency ideas as approved positioning.
claim_rules: Separate client claims, parent-group claims, regulator data, third-party rankings, and strategic judgement.
Use the narrowest claim that the evidence supports.
Name the source and date for market share, ranking, and performance claims.
Treat hypotheses as hypotheses until audience research or client data tests them.
Keep legal, regulatory, pricing, competition, cyber, data, and environmental claims under review before client-facing use.
Do not turn a proof point from one segment into a claim about the whole company.

legal: Claims touching market share, pricing, or competitive position require Legal and Regulatory review.
Environmental, social and governance claims must align with group-verified data.
The General Data Protection Regulation applies to audience targeting, campaign data, and influencer data handling.
The European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, Digital Services Act, and Digital Markets Act require awareness where relevant.
regulatory: The client operates under a national communications regulator.
Regulatory proceedings, outages, data security, and leadership-transition sensitivities carry crisis sensitivity.
Claims about communications markets, consumer pricing, competition position, and data handling need regulator-aware language.
confidentiality: The supplied brief excludes real commercial or retainer terms, and this pack must not publish those terms.
The supplied brief excludes unannounced strategic plans, and this pack must not turn them into findings.
The desk audit uses public sources; the deliverable withholds non-public financial, budget, retainer, and transition specifics unless the client clears them.
ai_use: Use only publicly grounded facts plus the sanitized brief.
Exclude leadership-transition specifics from artificial intelligence use.
Exclude real commercial or retainer terms from artificial intelligence use.
Exclude competitor-by-name intelligence from artificial intelligence use when it comes from non-public client material; public competitor sources may be used and named.
Treat prior unadopted agency positioning ideas as tone reference only, never approved positioning.
anonymization: The brief's rule to replace the client name with a generic stand-in is retired for this pack because the engagement declares Vivacom by name.
Individual names that are public in the desk audit may be used; non-public individuals stay masked as role titles.
Financial specifics, budgets, retainer terms, and excluded leadership-transition details stay masked as ranges, role titles, or to be confirmed.

Final sign-off sits with the chief executive officer and parent-group corporate communications function.

owner_decisions.question: What is the point of view we take on this client? This is yours to add: the desk audit gives you the material, but the angle is not the engine's to author.

Do we mirror the client's voice, or hold to house style? The volume's rule: mirror where strong, default to house style where not. When the client's voice is not strong enough, default to UP (United Partners) house style and flag the gap: an unclear, jargon-heavy or inflated corporate voice is frequently a symptom of the reputation problem, not a neutral choice.

alterations.instruction: any "market leader by revenue" line must always name the metric: the CRC 2024 report has Vivacom leading fixed internet, fixed voice and pay TV, while A1 leads mobile internet revenue and Yettel leads mobile voice revenue. Unqualified leadership stays out.

Sort it by the test in the question bank — who must approve (United Group and BC Partners, the CEO, parent-group communications), who must believe (employees, public-sector customers, media), and who must only not object (regulators, competitors). Where critics on pricing, contracts, outages and data pull against the advocates (United Group, partners, network testers), the narrative must carry a proof point, not a promise.

# What we need from you on the Pre-Engagement Briefing Pack

The AI (artificial intelligence) desk audit is done and the pack is drafted. These are the calls the method keeps for a person. Nothing after this step runs until the point of view on the hypothesis and the style calibration each carry an answer with your name against it.

How to answer: under each section write `Approved by: <name>` if the draft stands, or `Changed by: <name>` and what it should say instead. Both are decisions; only an approval settles a section.

Blocking the rest of the work: the point of view on the hypothesis, and the style calibration.

Not blocking: the question bank. The method drafts it here and tailors it during the later client-intake work, so it travels on as a draft. Say what you would change if you want it changed now; the run does not wait on it.

## How to use this review

Terms, context and next steps orient the reader.

### Terms

- Approved by — the operator's mark on a numbered section that the draft in it stands as written
- Changed by — the operator's mark on a numbered section that the draft in it is being replaced, followed by what it should say instead
- section — one of the numbered blocks below, each covering one part of the pre-engagement briefing pack the review is built from
- guided interview — the sequenced-prompt review mode the operator can choose instead of this page; the same content asked one section at a time

### Context

This is the operator-review page for the pre-engagement briefing pack. It travels with the pack as the second thing Phases 2 and 3 produce, and it lists the questions the operator has to answer before anything downstream advances.

### Next steps

Under each numbered section below, write `Approved by: <name>` if the draft stands, or `Changed by: <name>` and what it should say instead. Both are decisions; only an approval settles a section. Nothing after Phase 3 runs until the point of view on the hypothesis and the style calibration each carry an approved answer with a name against it. The question bank is recorded here and tailored in step two, so it does not hold the run.

## 1. Business Audit

Read the Business audit findings and gaps below. Do the findings hold up on the client you know, and is any gap the one that would change how you walk into the client conversation?

*Findings as drafted:*

- What the company does. Vivacom is a Bulgarian telecommunications provider serving households, businesses, and institutions (https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
- What the company does. Vivacom offers mobile voice, fixed voice, mobile broadband, fixed broadband, interactive TV, satellite TV, Internet of Things, smart-city, digital education, and cloud services (https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
- What the company does. Vivacom says it provides telecommunications solutions for private and business clients, including mobile and fixed voice, high-speed optical internet, satellite TV, interactive TV, and tailored offers for corporate clients (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- What the company does. United Group describes Vivacom as a leading provider of mobile, fixed broadband, and television services in Bulgaria (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
- What the company does. United Group said in 2020 that Vivacom was the first telecommunications company in Bulgaria and supplied fibre broadband, mobile communications, and digital TV to private and commercial customers (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/).
- What the company does. Vivacom says its own infrastructure includes mobile, fixed, terrestrial, copper, and satellite assets (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- What the company does. Vivacom says its 5G network covers 92% of Bulgaria’s population, its 4G LTE network covers 99.95%, and its 2G and 3G networks cover 99.99% (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- What the company does. Vivacom says its fixed network covers 1.6 million homes and includes the first and only 10 GIGA network in Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- What the company does. Vivacom says it has more than 200 own retail stores across Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- Its business model. Vivacom serves both private and business customers with mobile and fixed voice, high-speed fixed broadband, mobile broadband, interactive TV, satellite TV, Internet of Things, smart-city, digital education, and cloud services (https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
- Its business model. Vivacom’s revenue model is a telecom bundle model built around mobile, fixed broadband, fixed voice, pay TV, devices, business services, and public-sector solutions (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/).
- Its business model. United Group says Vivacom has backed the shift to IPTV through EON, a TV product developed by United Cloud, and that IPTV has passed one million households nationally (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
- Its business model. Netcracker says Vivacom uses Netcracker Revenue Management for billing, invoicing, and other revenue-related processes across postpaid mobile and fixed lines for B2C and B2B customers (https://www.netcracker.com/news/press-releases/netcracker-and-vivacom-extend-long-term-partnership-for-innovative-it-modernization-program).
- Its business model. United Group completed the acquisition of Bulsatcom in February 2024, adding a direct-to-home satellite TV and broadband internet business in Bulgaria to the group’s Bulgarian perimeter (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom).
- Its performance. Vivacom says it has invested nearly BGN 3 billion in technology, innovation, human resources, and the Bulgarian economy; this pass found no independent source that restates the full BGN 3 billion figure (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- Its performance. Vivacom says more than 2 million customers use more than 5.5 million services from the company; this pass found no independent source that restates those exact customer and service counts (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- Its performance. CRC’s 2024 Annual Report says Vivacom held 37.1% of fixed Internet access retail revenue in 2024, up 8.3 percentage points from 2023 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. CRC’s 2024 Annual Report notes that Bulsatcom EOOD was incorporated into Vivacom Bulgaria EAD as of 10 July 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. United Group said on 15 July 2026 that Bulgaria’s telecom market grew close to 5% in the prior year to EUR 2.16 billion and that market Internet revenue rose more than 9% to EUR 1.21 billion (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
- Its performance. United Group said on 15 July 2026 that Vivacom grew its mobile service-revenue share over the prior year (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
- Its performance. United Group said in 2020 that Vivacom had been Bulgaria’s largest domestic operator by revenue for the previous seven years (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/).
- Its leadership. Vivacom’s management page names Asen Velikov as member of the management board and chief executive officer (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip).
- Its leadership. United Group’s leadership page says Asen Velikov is both chief executive officer and chief financial officer of Vivacom, joined the company in 1999, became chief financial officer in 2013, and has been a management-board member since 2014 (https://united.group/leadership/asen-velikov/).
- Its leadership. Vivacom’s management page names Nikolay Gavrilov as management-board member and chief technical officer (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip).
- Its leadership. Vivacom’s management page names Stoyan Karanlakov as management-board member and chief commercial officer, with the role taken on 15 September 2021 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip).
- Its leadership. Vivacom’s management page names Ognyan Toshmakov as management-board member and chief financial officer from 13 July 2026 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip).
- Its leadership. Vivacom’s management page names Ivo Zlatev as management-board member and chief legal officer, in that role since 2017 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/ekip).
- Its leadership. SeeNews reported on 5 August 2025 that United Group appointed Asen Velikov as CEO, replacing Nikolai Andreev, who was dismissed (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-vivacom-names-ceo-1279653).
- Its leadership. SeeNews reported that Stan Miller was named chair of Vivacom’s supervisory board, Spas Rusev and Stan Miller were appointed as new board members, and Nikolaos Statopoulos was re-elected for five years (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-vivacom-names-ceo-1279653).
- Its ownership. Vivacom says it has been part of United Group since 2020 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- Its ownership. United Group says it completed the acquisition of Vivacom on 31 July 2020 after European Commission approval in April 2020 and a signed agreement in November 2019 (https://united.group/united-group-welcomes-vivacom-the-largest-telecom-operator-in-bulgaria/).
- Its ownership. Schoenherr says the 2020 United Group acquisition of Vivacom was valued at EUR 1.2 billion and was Bulgaria’s largest 2019 deal by value and asset size (https://schoenherr.eu/content/bulgaria-schoenherr-advises-united-group-on-eur-1-2-bln-acquisition-of-vivacom).
- Its ownership. United Group says it is majority owned by BC Partners, and BC Partners says the group is majority owned by BC Partners (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom; https://www.bcpartners.com/portfolio/united-group/).
- Its ownership. Vivacom says it is the successor to BTC, the first telecommunications company in Bulgaria, and says BTC moved from a long state-owned period to privatization in 2004 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata).
- Its ownership. Private Equity International reported that Advent’s 2004 BTC agreement covered a EUR 230 million purchase price plus a EUR 50 million capital increase (https://www.privateequityinternational.com/advent-finally-wins-bulgarian-telco/).
- Its ownership. A SeeNews telecom sector report says the 2004 privatization sale of a 65% BTC stake was formally completed in June 2004, with Vienna-registered Viva Ventures GmbH remitting EUR 280 million (https://cdn.seenews.com/reports/TELECOMMUNICATIONS_Telecommunications%20Sector%20-%20Bulgaria%20%282006%29.pdf).
- Its ownership. The Bulgarian Industrial Association reported that NEF Telecom Bulgaria sold a 93.99% stake in Vivacom to Viva Telecom Bulgaria in 2012 (https://en.bia-bg.com/service/view/14419/).
- Its ownership. Developing Telecoms reported that Vivacom was sold at auction in November 2015 for about EUR 730 million (https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/6155-bulgarian-operator-vivacom-acquired-at-auction-for-730m.html).
- Recent news. United Group said on 15 July 2026 that it would keep backing Vivacom’s investment in fibre, 5G, and EON as Bulgaria’s telecom market expanded (https://united.group/united-group-backs-vivacoms-growth-as-bulgaria-telecoms-market-expands/).
- Recent news. Netcracker announced on 11 February 2026 that Vivacom extended its long-term partnership for an IT modernization program and would upgrade to the latest Netcracker Revenue Management platform (https://www.netcracker.com/news/press-releases/netcracker-and-vivacom-extend-long-term-partnership-for-innovative-it-modernization-program).
- Recent news. SeeNews reported on 18 May 2026 that United Group was considering selling some or all Bulgarian assets, including Vivacom’s fixed network and Nova Broadcasting Group; this was reported as a media report, not as a confirmed United Group announcement (https://seenews.com/news/see-focused-united-group-mulls-selling-bulgarian-assets-report-1294890).
- Recent news. Vivacom published an 8 August 2025 item showing Asen Velikov in the public CEO role during a meeting with summer interns (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/stazhantite-na-vivacom-v-razgovor-s-glavniya-izpalnitelen-direktor-asen-velikov).
- Recent news. SeeNews reported on 5 August 2025 that United Group appointed Asen Velikov as CEO and changed Vivacom’s supervisory board (https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-vivacom-names-ceo-1279653).
- Recent news. United Group completed the Bulsatcom acquisition on 27 February 2024, and CRC’s 2024 Annual Report says Bulsatcom EOOD was incorporated into Vivacom Bulgaria EAD on 10 July 2024 (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its annual report or investor materials. Vivacom has public integrated annual reports on its own site, including the 2019 Integrated Report and a 2020 web report; this pass did not find a newer Vivacom stand-alone annual report page (https://www.vivacom.bg/bg/files/17826-integrated-report-2019.pdf; https://www.vivacom.bg/web/catalog/sustainableen/index.html).
- Its annual report or investor materials. United Group has an investor site with sections for quarterly reports, annual reports, presentations, shareholder structure, bonds, and credit rating, but the fetched public HTML did not expose the report files in this pass (https://investors.united.group/).
- Its annual report or investor materials. United Group’s 9M 2025 investor news says revenue increased 3% year on year to EUR 2.0 billion, last-twelve-month revenue reached EUR 2.7 billion, adjusted EBITDAal grew 7% to about EUR 680 million, and last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDAal reached EUR 909 million (https://united.group/united-group-b-v-continues-to-deliver-strong-growth-in-the-third-quarter-of-2025/).
- Its annual report or investor materials. United Group’s 2023 results release says the group delivered EUR 2.791 billion of revenue, EUR 988 million of EBITDAal, a 35% EBITDAal margin, and year-end net debt to adjusted EBITDAal of 4.20x (https://united.group/united-group-b-v-continues-successful-growth-path-in-2023-with-record-results/).
- Engagement trigger. The supplied brief says the engagement is a corporate brand and corporate communications strategy from a blank slate, with no approved corporate brand strategy, positioning, narrative, or pillar architecture in place (sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md). (bears on: the ask itself -- what is wanted, who decides, how success is defined)
- Strategic business setting. The supplied brief says Vivacom is stable and profitable but works in a mature, saturated, price-pressured market where the three main operators have moved toward similar claims (sanitized-telecom-blank-slate-brief.md). (bears on: Business problem / organizational objective)
- Self-claim verdict. Vivacom calls itself "Vivacom е иноватор"; AmCham independently confirms the breadth of the offer but does not verify the word innovator (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://amcham.bg/member/vivacom/). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)
- Network proof guardrail. Vivacom says its 5G network has "най-голямо покритие в България"; United Group independently says it developed the country’s largest 5G network after entering Bulgaria in 2020, so the coverage claim is corroborated at group level (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini/united-group-compretes-the-acquisition-of-bulsatcom). (bears on: Constraints and guardrails -- what cannot be said, claimed or processed)
- Fixed-network claim. Vivacom says its fixed fibre network is "най-бързата оптична мрежа в България" and points to CRC tariff-comparison data dated 23 May 2025; this pass did not independently reproduce the CRC comparison output, so the exact speed ranking needs proof capture before use in client text (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata). (bears on: Baseline data & measurement access)
- Municipal customer base. Vivacom says it works with more than 130 Bulgarian municipalities through smart-city services, which bears on public-sector and local-government audiences (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata). (bears on: Priority audiences & current state)
- CSR proof pool. Vivacom says it has donated more than BGN 6 million over 15 years for more than 300 causes and more than 200 organizations; this is a CSR proof pool, but this pass did not find an independent public tally for those figures (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata). (bears on: Programme, narrative and channels -- the story, the spokespeople, what has worked)
- What the company does. SeeNews says Vivacom provides professional internet and data services, radio and television data transfer, leased lines, VoIP, and public payphones, in addition to fixed-line telephony, mobile communications, internet, and digital TV (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- What the company does. Vivacom’s 2018 Annual Activities Report says Vivacom develops, operates, and maintains national fixed and mobile networks and a data system for Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf). The same report says Vivacom owned Plana teleport, serving orbital positions in Europe, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf).
- What the company does. Vivacom’s 2018 Annual Activities Report says NURTS Group was a Vivacom-owned provider of radio and television broadcasting, terrestrial and satellite signal transmission, and colocation services in Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf). The same report says NURTS Group owned and operated more than 500 radio and television stations across Bulgaria (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf).
- What the company does. SeeNews says Vivacom owned and operated the Plana Teleport satellite facility with 40 antennae at the end of 2016 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- Its business model. SeeNews says Vivacom provides fixed-line telephony, mobile communications, internet, professional internet and data services, radio and television data transfer, leased lines, VoIP, public payphones, and digital TV (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- Its business model. CRC says 6,415,737 mobile voice subscribers in Bulgaria used the service in a package with other electronic communications services at 31 December 2024, equal to 80.4% of mobile voice subscribers (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC’s Vivacom market-share tables for fixed internet, mobile internet, and pay TV count subscribers and revenue from bundled services, which confirms that bundled access is central to the market model Vivacom competes in (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its business model. Broadband TV News reported on 17 March 2026 that Vivacom added BBC First and BBC Earth to EON in Bulgaria (https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2026/03/17/vivacom-adds-bbc-first-and-bbc-earth-to-eon-in-bulgaria/). Broadband TV News reported that BBC First was added to EON Premium and BBC Earth to EON Full and EON Premium, showing package-tier content as part of the TV offer (https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2026/03/17/vivacom-adds-bbc-first-and-bbc-earth-to-eon-in-bulgaria/).
- Its business model. SeeNews says Vivacom signed a EUR 1.5 million deal with Burgas municipality in March 2020 for video-surveillance upgrade and expansion (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525). SeeNews says Vivacom and Bulgaria’s labour ministry signed 10 telecommunications-service contracts worth BGN 1.75 million in October 2019 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- Its performance. SeeNews lists Vivacom Bulgaria EAD’s 2024 revenue as BGN 1,429,290,000, 2024 profit as BGN 234,941,000, 2024 assets as BGN 2,693,006,000, and employees as 4,756 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- Its performance. CRC says Vivacom held second place in Bulgarian retail mobile voice in 2024 by both subscribers and revenue (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC says Vivacom’s mobile voice revenue share rose from 25.4% in 2020 to 32.0% in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC says Vivacom was the only mobile operator whose subscriber share increased every year from 2020 to 2024, adding 4.3 percentage points over the period (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. CRC says Vivacom held 56.5% of fixed voice lines and 82.2% of fixed voice subscriber revenue in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC says Vivacom was the only undertaking declaring public payphone activity in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. CRC says Vivacom held 36.7% of retail mobile internet access subscribers and 28.2% of mobile internet access revenue in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC says A1 remained the mobile internet revenue leader with 42.1% in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. CRC says Vivacom held 59.6% of Bulgarian retail pay-TV subscribers and 56.5% of pay-TV revenue in 2024 (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf). CRC says Vivacom’s pay-TV shares grew mainly because Bulsatcom and TVN Distribution Bulgaria were incorporated into Vivacom (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).
- Its performance. Vivacom’s 2018 Annual Activities Report says it served 3.071 million mobile subscribers, 689,000 fixed telephony subscribers, 444,000 fixed broadband subscribers, and 468,000 fixed pay-TV subscribers at 31 December 2018 (https://www.vivacom.bg/web/files/financial_reports/95/document/Vivacom_report_2018.pdf).
- Its leadership. United Group’s 28 July 2026 H1 operations update says Vivacom CEO Asen Velikov joined European business leaders in launching the Sofia Initiative, which called for more investment in digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence, and next-generation connectivity across Europe (https://united.group/updates-from-united-groups-operations-h1-2026/).
- Its leadership. United Group appointed Janet Zaharieva as Group Director Public Policy and Corporate Affairs while she also remains Chief Public Policy and European Affairs at Vivacom (https://united.group/united-group-strengthens-its-leadership-team/). United Group says Zaharieva has 28 years in communications, media, and ICT, and has been part of Vivacom leadership since 2010 (https://united.group/united-group-strengthens-its-leadership-team/).
- Its ownership. SeeNews lists Vivacom Bulgaria EAD’s direct owner as Slovenia Broadband SARL with a 100% direct holding (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525). SeeNews lists Slovenia Broadband SARL as a Luxembourg company (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).
- Its ownership. SeeNews says United Group Bulgaria EOOD became the sole owner on 20 July 2022 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525). SeeNews says Slovenia Broadband SARL acquired 100% of Bulgarian Telecommunications Company EAD on 13 September 2022 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525). SeeNews says the company changed its name to Vivacom Bulgaria EAD on 5 October 2022 (https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525).

Vivacom says it is the successor to BTC, Bulgaria's first telecommunications company. In 2004, the state sold 65% of BTC to Viva Ventures, a unit of Advent International; SeeNews records the price as EUR 275.356 million, while Novinite records a widely cited EUR 230 million sale figure. BTC Mobile launched services under the vivatel brand in November 2005. BTC and vivatel combined under the Vivacom brand in 2009. (https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata; https://seenews.com/companies/profile/vivacom-bulgaria-ead-formerly-known-as-bulgarian-telecommunications-company-ead-4525; https://www.novinite.com/articles/139418/Bulgaria%2BDefeated%2Bin%2BCourt%2Bby%2BViva%2BVentures%2Bover%2BTelco%2BDeal) (bears on: business and organizational context)

VTB Capital secured a majority stake in 2015 for EUR 130 million. United Group agreed in 2019 to acquire Vivacom for a reported EUR 1.2 billion, and the deal closed in 2020. Telecom and adjacent digital activity in Bulgaria is also affected by the General Data Protection Regulation, Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Cybersecurity Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, NIS2 Directive and Critical Entity Resilience Directive; this confirms the supplied brief’s legal and AI-policy constraints (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).
- Regulatory context. The Communications Regulation Commission is the independent telecom regulator; the Ministry of Transport and Communications and Ministry of e-Government set ICT, digital administration and cybersecurity policy; the National Radio Frequency Spectrum Council handles national spectrum-planning proposals (https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/).

CRC Decision No. 220 of 30 July 2024 found no effective competition in wholesale access to passive physical infrastructure, named Vivacom as having significant individual impact, and imposed access, non-discrimination, transparency, reference-offer and price-control duties (https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf).

Essential-entity penalties can reach EUR 10 million or 2% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, with manager liability also introduced (https://www.schoenherr.eu/content/bulgaria-implements-nis-2-directive-key-changes-to-the-cybersecurity-act).
