compose-research-insight-pack.output:
# Research & Insight Pack

One pack, not five disconnected audits. Every finding shows where it came from -- for a web finding, a URL (uniform resource locator); for supplied material, the place in the pack it came from. A finding this engine could not source from the material it was given says so in its own row rather than being presented as research. The AI (artificial intelligence) drafts each audit and a strategist validates and interprets it. The Sweet Spot the pack ends on names the client's USP (unique selling proposition) at the intersection with the insight nobody else has leveraged yet.

## Client Style Note

Captured from the client's own published communications. Every client-facing deliverable is written to this voice -- its tone, typical sentence length, vocabulary, self-reference, and signature do/don't words.

- **tone:** Vivacom's own voice is direct, service-led, and confident. It often opens with the customer benefit, then supports it with network scale, product detail, or programme proof.
- **sentence length:** The client uses mostly short to medium sentences in public-facing copy, with longer sentences when it lists service features, coverage figures, or programme details.
- **vocabulary:** The client's vocabulary centres on connectivity, customers, digital services, innovation, technology, coverage, speed, education, skills, entertainment, support, and Bulgaria's digital development.
- **self reference:** Vivacom refers to itself by the brand name, by the company name, and through first-person plural forms in Bulgarian when it wants a warmer social or employer tone.
- **signature do words:** customers, digital services, connectivity, coverage, technology, innovation, education, skills, support, Bulgaria
- **signature dont words:** world-class, best-in-class, game-changing, state utility, former monopoly, price war, political positioning
- **sources:** https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/za-kompaniyata, https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/novini, https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/sotsialna-otgovornost, https://www.vivacom.bg/za-nas/karieri, https://www.vivacom.bg/pomosht/kontakti, https://www.vivacom.bg/business/satelitni-uslugi
- **long form voice:** Not yet calibrated: no long-form writing of the client's own has been read.
- **voice evidence read:** short-form copy only — long-form voice not yet calibrated

## Clear, professional communication language

Every Research document meets the clear, professional communication language standard. The wording is checked sentence by sentence and the whole text is checked end to end, against the rules named in the language standard.

**Wording rules**
- **Plain words:** Use the everyday word, not the impressive one. No jargon. No acronym without its meaning at first use. No filler.
- **Short sentences:** One idea per sentence. Active voice. If a sentence needs a second read, rewrite it.
- **Concrete, not abstract:** Say what happens, who does it, and by when. Replace vague claims with facts.
- **Proof, not adjectives:** Every claim carries evidence. Delete superlatives that carry none.
- **Confident, not inflated:** Assured, warm but not casual, direct. No hedging that hides a decision; no claim that outruns its proof.
- **One name per thing:** Call the same thing by the same name in every document. Never rename a concept midway.
- **Reader's language, not the method's:** Client-facing documents are written in the reader's language, not the method's. No process term reaches a client page unexplained.

**Whole-text rules**
- **One clear purpose:** The reader knows in the first paragraph what this document is and what it is for.
- **Headline first:** Every section starts with its point, then the support beneath it. A busy reader who reads only the headings still gets the story.
- **Logical flow:** Sections follow one order of thought. Each builds on the one before. No jumps, no repeats.
- **Right length:** As short as the content allows. Anything that supports but does not advance the argument goes to an appendix.
- **Short paragraphs:** One idea per paragraph. If a paragraph runs long, split it. A wall of text goes back.
- **Visual clarity:** Tables for comparisons, short lists for sequences, bold sparingly. White space is part of the writing.
- **Self-contained:** A new reader can use the document without a briefing. Terms, context and next steps are inside it.

## Accountable review gates

Research writes the assignment on every pack so the discipline check reads a real owner next to every gate that reviews its output.

| review gate | accountable owner |
| --- | --- |
| Research pack review | United Partners strategy lead |
| Sourcing & figures audit | United Partners quality lead |
| Insight review board | United Partners head of insight |

## Primary reputation risks

Research names the primary reputation risks on every pack so the discipline check reads them against the work rather than inferring them from adjacent context.

- overclaim
- inconsistency
- ambiguity

## Do not say

Research works only from the material it was handed. The three shapes of invention the pack refuses are named here, each with why the pack refuses it.

| do not say | why |
| --- | --- |
| invented clients | Research works only from the material it was handed; a client relationship, quote or reference the material does not carry cannot be attributed to a client. |
| invented metrics | No number, percentage, ranking or share of voice enters the pack unless a source in the supplied material carries it. No invented figures, at all, for any reason. |
| invented claims | A statement about the market, the audience or the client is only Research when a source in the supplied material grounds it. A finding Research could not source says so in its own row rather than being presented as a claim. |

## Executive summary

What a reader gets if they read nothing else. Each finding carries what it changes.

1. **Vivacom has strong infrastructure proof, but that proof does not yet add up to one trusted national role.**
   _26 August 2026; 2024_ · source: Approved Brief, Reputation problem / opportunity; https://crc.bg/files/Annual_Report_CRC_2024_EN.pdf · confidence: high
   **So what.** The strategy should make Vivacom useful in Bulgarian daily life, not simply bigger or more advanced than competitors.

2. **Vivacom leads or performs strongly in fixed internet, pay TV (television), coverage and satellite, but it does not lead every mobile or internet measure.**
   _15/12/2025; January 2026_ · source: https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/; https://insights.opensignal.com/reports/2026/01/bulgaria/mobile-network-experience · confidence: high
   **So what.** The strategy must use narrow proof-led claims and avoid broad market-leader language.

3. **Vivacom leads article volume in the Q1 2026 three-operator media set, but much of that volume is planned public relations with weak audience response.**
   _Q1 2026_ · source: https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war · confidence: medium
   **So what.** The channel strategy should optimise for trusted response and proof recall, not for volume.

4. **Customer friction is a live reputation constraint through app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract and pricing disputes, outages and data-protection enforcement.**
   _no date recorded; no date recorded; 19 March 2025; 27 March 2025_ · source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.vivacom.bg; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en&id=bg.vivacom.mobile; https://www.bta.bg/en/news/economy/854994-supreme-administrative-court-upholds-consumer-protection-commission-s-order-agai; https://www.linklaters.com/en/insights/data-protected/data-protected---bulgaria · confidence: high
   **So what.** A warm story will fail unless it shows practical service improvement and fairness, not only emotion.

5. **The live sale and divestment context keeps leadership cautious and makes parent-group approval important.**
   _no date recorded; May 18, 2026_ · source: Step 2 Debrief; https://seenews.com/news/see-focused-united-group-mulls-selling-bulgarian-assets-report-1294890 · confidence: medium
   **So what.** The strategy needs an internal line leaders can use safely before it becomes an external platform.

**0 findings are not sourced from the supplied material.** They are recorded so they can be checked, not so they can be used.

## Patterns

The recurring shapes across the pack, each pointing to the ownable space ingredient it feeds. This is how Research organizes the answers into patterns that point to an ownable space, so Discovery does not have to reconstruct the ownable space from unsorted findings.

| pattern | evidence | points to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vivacom has proof of scale, but scale also creates scrutiny. | This pattern appears in Trusted National Role, Regulatory And Issues Pressure, and Competitive audit. | Client priorities or USP |
| Volume does not equal trust. | This pattern appears in Social media audit, Mainstream media audit, and Reputation read: Share of voice on the themes that matter, not just volume. | Unleveraged insight |
| The warm story must pass through service proof. | This pattern appears in Customer Warmth Gap, Reputation read: The say-do gap, and Persona: Maya. | Unleveraged insight |
| Vivacom's safer white space is useful national outcomes, not broad technology leadership. | This pattern appears in Competitive White Space, Proof-Led Claim Boundaries, and PESTLE (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental) Technological. | Client priorities or USP |

## Benchmarks

The comparative reference points -- where the client stands against a peer, a norm, or itself over time -- each pointing to the ownable space ingredient it feeds.

| benchmark | reference | us | points to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fixed internet subscriber position | A1 at 29.9% of fixed internet subscribers, source: https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/ | Vivacom is ahead at 39.4% in 2024. | Client priorities or USP |
| Mobile network proof | A1 fastest and Yettel strongest on reliability and time on network, source: https://insights.opensignal.com/reports/2026/01/bulgaria/mobile-network-experience | Vivacom wins coverage experience, so it should claim coverage rather than total mobile leadership. | Unleveraged insight |
| Social engagement | A1 leads Q1 2026 social engagement in Pikasa's three-operator set, source: https://pikasa.ai/post/149/the-platform-bet-how-bulgarian-telecoms-are-winning-and-losing-the-attention-war | Vivacom leads press volume but trails engagement, which shows a response gap. | Unleveraged insight |
| Pay-TV position | A1 is the other major pay-TV company, source: https://iclg.com/practice-areas/telecoms-media-and-internet-laws-and-regulations/bulgaria/ | Vivacom leads with about 60% of subscribers in 2024. | Client priorities or USP |
| Customer-review warning signal | App stores and Trustpilot show visible service criticism, source: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en&id=bg.vivacom.mobile and https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.vivacom.bg | Vivacom has large self-care touchpoints but must show service improvement before warmth can land. | Unleveraged insight |

## The ownable space — the Sweet Spot at the intersection

The Sweet Spot the Synthesize phase finds at the intersection of client priorities/USP and unleveraged insight, and hands to strategist-owned Discovery for the Killer Insight. The patterns and benchmarks above feed the two ingredients named here; a strategist, not the engine, crosses them into the Killer Insight in Discovery.

- **Client priorities or USP.** Vivacom's priority is to build one warmer, proof-led corporate story that moves it from activity-led presence to a trusted national role. Its usable strength is the mix of fixed internet, pay TV, coverage, satellite, EON (a Vivacom interactive television product line), public-sector work and skills programmes.
- **Unleveraged insight.** Vivacom already has proof of usefulness, but it is scattered across products, infrastructure and programmes. The unused opportunity is to turn that proof into everyday Bulgarian outcomes that existing customers, employees and urban audiences can believe.

## Buckets & Questions

Each bucket answers one sharp question, and each says what the answer would change.

### Trusted National Role

**Question.** Can Vivacom turn infrastructure scale into a trusted role in Bulgaria's daily digital progress?

**So what.** The strategy should make national usefulness the centre of the story, with named proof by place, service or audience.

# Killer Insight Cards

16 candidates were written and screened; 7 survived; 1 are put forward as cards. Volume first, then judgment.

**Nobody has selected the insight yet.** The volume reserves that for a person: the final insight is chosen, defined and defended by a human, and this engine does not author it on autopilot.

## Card 1

**Vivacom's corporate story starts with people who already use it. They will not believe a warmer national role until they see Vivacom make the paid relationship feel clearer, fairer and easier to live with.**

**Type.** intuitive

**The 5 T's.** True: pass — The approved brief names existing customers as the primary first-believer audience and says they are among the hardest to win. · Tacit: pass — It makes explicit that preference must start with current customer belief, not public awareness alone. · Touches the heart: pass — It speaks to the everyday feeling of whether a service provider is fair and useful. · Tension: pass — It contrasts the paid relationship with the need to earn trust again. · Triggers action: pass — It prioritises customer-facing proof, service language and fairness before broader corporate campaigning.

**The tension.** Vivacom is functionally important in daily life, but the people closest to it can still feel exposed to billing, service and contract friction.

**The audience it is about.** Existing customers who judge Vivacom through bills, outages, app payments, support and contract clarity.
**Audience personas.** Maya

**The opportunity it opens.** Turn the corporate story into a proof-led service relationship: clearer bills, easier app journeys, visible fixes, named support improvements and claims that customers can verify in their own lives.

**What the audience truly cares about.** Maya wants reliable service, clear billing, simple help and fewer surprises.

**The company's ownable truth.** Vivacom touches home internet, mobile, television and support in one daily relationship, and it has the fixed internet, pay TV, coverage and service proof to make that relationship feel useful.

**Evidence.** The approved brief names existing customers as the primary first-believer audience and says they are among the hardest to win. The same brief says Vivacom leads on functional and reliability attributes but under-indexes on warmth, while the research records customer friction in app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract penalties, outages and data-protection pressure.
#### The evidence beneath it

| what the evidence shows | source & standing |
| --- | --- |
| Existing customers are the primary first-believer audience and are hard to win after integrations and service changes. | Approved Brief, Priority audiences · dated · high |
| Vivacom leads on functional and reliability attributes but under-indexes on warmth, and its lead disappears among Gen Z. | Approved Brief, Reputation problem / opportunity · dated · high |
| Visible customer friction appears in app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract and pricing disputes, outages and data-protection enforcement. | Research & Insight Pack, Executive summary; Customer Warmth Gap; Regulatory And Issues Pressure · dated · high |


**So what.** The strategy should not open with national scale. It should open with proof that Vivacom is useful and fair in the daily moments customers already judge.

# The screening

Every candidate against the five T's and the distinctiveness check. A candidate is kept only when all five hold and no competitor could equally claim it.

| candidate | kind | True | Tacit | Touches the heart | Tension | Triggers action | distinctive | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing customers will not warm to Vivacom because it feels bigger; they will warm to Vivacom when its scale makes small daily problems feel easier, fairer and less surprising. | intuitive | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| Vivacom's strongest national story is not technology leadership; it is making digital life in Bulgaria work in the places and moments people can name. | intuitive | pass | pass | conditional | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| Vivacom should stop trying to win attention with more proof and start making fewer proofs easier to believe. | intuitive | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| Vivacom can only claim a trusted national role if it treats service friction as part of the story, not as noise outside the story. | empirical | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| The first audience for Vivacom's corporate story is not the market; it is the customer who already pays and still needs a reason to believe the company is on their side. | intuitive | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| Vivacom's sale uncertainty makes silence feel safer inside the company, but silence is exactly what stops employees from carrying the story outside it. | intuitive | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | yes | kept |
| Vivacom's biggest risk is not being challenged for weakness; it is being challenged for claiming strength too broadly. | empirical | pass | pass | fail | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Bulgaria's digital-skills gap gives Vivacom a public-benefit role beyond connectivity. | empirical | pass | partial | conditional | partial | pass | no | discarded |
| A1 can own speed and Yettel can own certified quality; Vivacom can own coverage people can feel in daily life. | empirical | pass | partial | partial | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Vivacom's old BTK association is best beaten by showing transformation through today's useful services, not by arguing with the past. | intuitive | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Municipal projects can make Vivacom's national role visible because they turn network scale into citizen services. | empirical | pass | partial | conditional | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| The corporate story should make Legal a creative partner, because Vivacom's most useful claims are also the claims most likely to be scrutinised. | intuitive | pass | pass | fail | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Vivacom's youth problem is not that Gen Z knows too little about technology; it is that functional strength does not yet feel like a modern, human relationship. | intuitive | partial | pass | conditional | pass | partial | yes | discarded |
| Vivacom should make the app a trust stage, because My Vivacom is where the promise of useful digital life is tested most often. | empirical | partial | pass | partial | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Vivacom's proof pool is wide enough to tell one national story, but only if every proof is attached to one reader benefit. | intuitive | pass | pass | partial | pass | pass | no | discarded |
| Vivacom does not need a softer voice first; it needs harder evidence of being easier to live with. | intuitive | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | yes | kept |

# The extraction process — seven steps

1. Immerse — absorb the research pack, the filled buckets, the audits, the reputation read
2. Generate volume — write many candidates, empirical and intuitive; do not edit yet
3. So-What ladder — push each promising candidate up the pyramid with repeated 'so what?'
4. Screen — test each against the five T's and discard what fails any of them
5. Find the Sweet Spot — the ownable truth, an insight not yet leveraged, what the audience truly cares about
6. Distinctiveness Gate — reject anything a competitor could also claim, or the obvious white space everyone sees
7. Distil — land one to three Killer Insights, no more

# Two kinds of insight — and why you need both

| | what it is | proven by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empirical insight | Grounded in data acquired through research methods | The data itself |
| Intuitive insight | Grounded in knowing or sensing, without a rational process | Observation and qualitative evidence — it still needs backup |

**The UP principle.** It is through science that we prove, but through intuition that we discover. The strongest Killer Insights pair an intuitive human truth with empirical proof — the discovery and the evidence together.

# The climb — from data to insight

Insight is a level on a ladder, reached by disciplined questioning — not a lucky thought.

| level | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Raw, uncontextualised facts ("sales rose 23%") |
| Information | Data organised & compared ("23% — 5 points above target, 8 below history") |
| Insight | What it means, strategically ("the growth is masking a loyalty problem") |
| Foresight | What it signals for the future ("expect margin pressure in 12 months") |

**The tool that climbs it: the So What? test.** For every finding ask "so what?" and keep asking until you reach genuine meaning. Guard against the five traps:

- correlation mistaken for causation
- confirmation bias
- volume mistaken for significance
- the missing counterfactual
- outliers mistaken for trends

# The Sweet Spot

An insight sits where all three meet:

- the company's ownable truth
- an insight not yet leveraged
- what the audience truly cares about

# Step 5B · Validate the insight

A distinctive, contrarian insight cannot lock until it is tested against the real audience. Distinctiveness and wrongness look identical until tested.

## Validating card 1

**How contrarian.** This cuts against the instinct to use corporate scale, innovation or national importance as the first trust claim. It says the national role is earned from the customer relationship outward, not announced from the company outward.

**What would validate it.** Ask current Vivacom customers who have used support, the app or billing in the last six months to compare two story routes: national digital progress first, or daily service usefulness first. The insight is confirmed if they trust and recall the daily-service route more, and describe it as more believable. It is refined if they want national proof only after a specific customer benefit. It is rejected if they find the national-progress route more credible and motivating without service proof.

**Verdict.** Confirm · Refine · Reject — none recorded. The test has not been run.


# Open — waiting on a person

- **Which of these is the insight?** — not yet decided; no owner recorded.
- **What did the audience say?** — the validation test has not been run, so no verdict is recorded.

# Insight mini-board — report

**Outcome: CLEARS the Board.** only low concerns stand.

Rule applied: Proceeds to the human ship gate with the Board report attached.

Three personas, convened at step 5B against the insight alone, to kill a weak insight before a whole strategy is built on it. The Competitor asks whether they could claim it word for word, the Target Audience whether they recognise themselves in it, the Activist what it looks like turned over. It is not the pre-ship board and it does not clear the work; it stops one thing from being built on.

Convened at step 5B: The Competitor · The Target Audience · The Hostile Stakeholder / Activist

## The verdicts

| persona | position | verdict | findings that survived the referee |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The Competitor | I can say that too. | PASS | 0 |
| The Target Audience | Why do I care? I don't believe you. | CONCERN | 2 |
| The Hostile Stakeholder / Activist | Here's how this blows up. | PASS | 0 |

## The findings

### 1. The Target Audience — Medium

**Finding.** Card 1 states the warmth barrier as a settled audience truth rather than a hypothesis still awaiting customer validation.

**Quoted target.** "Existing customers will not warm to Vivacom because it is large."

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite as a testable hypothesis: existing customers may not warm to Vivacom through scale alone; validate whether household-service proof changes belief.

### 2. The Target Audience — Medium

**Finding.** The card names what Maya cares about as established, but the pack says direct audience research has not yet been run.

**Quoted target.** "Maya wants reliable service, clear billing, simple help and fewer surprises."

**Suggested fix.** Keep this as the proposed validation language for customer interviews, then replace it with the audience's own words after testing.

## Struck by the referee

No attack counts unless it quotes the exact target. 0 were discarded before triage.


## How the findings were triaged

The system — not the operator — triages by these fixed rules. The one that fired is marked; the rest are shown so the outcome can be read against what did not happen.

| condition | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Any CRITICAL finding (legal red line, factual falsehood, greenwashing, reputational landmine) | HARD BLOCK — fix before anything else, regardless of all other verdicts |
| Competitor returns BLOCK on distinctiveness | RETURN to Insight/Strategy — a table-stakes strategy cannot ship |
| Target Audience returns BLOCK (insight not held / unvalidated) | RETURN to Insight — trigger M7 validation |
| ≥ 2 High concerns, or ≥ 4 Medium | MUST REVISE — auto-revise loop |
| **Only Low concerns, or all PASS** | CLEARS the Board → proceeds to the human ship gate with the Board report attached |

## The review loop

1. Draft
2. Attack
3. Referee
4. Triage
5. Fix
6. Re-review
7. Clear

Bounded to 3 rounds. Round 1 of 3 ran here. If it still cannot clear, it escalates to a human — the one place seniority is invoked, and only on genuinely hard deadlocks.

## Keeping the Board honest

It is AI, so it can flatter or hallucinate.

- **Grounding.** Each persona is fed real data, not imagination — the competitor's real positioning, the client's real record, actual audience evidence.
- **Specificity requirement.** No attack counts unless it quotes the exact target; the referee discards the rest.
- **Severity calibration.** Anchored to worked examples so verdicts are consistent run to run — no drifting standards.
- **Validate the validators.** Periodically check the Board's findings against real senior reviews: does it catch what seniors catch, without crying wolf?

## Operator-independence

The operator never scores the Board and never adjudicates a finding. The triage above is a fixed rule, not a judgement, so a novice and a veteran get the same scrutiny and the same fix set.

# Strategy One-Pager

The one page everything else flows from. A gap here is a gap in the thinking.

**No approach has been chosen.** The options are below with their evaluation; the choice belongs to a person and no owner is recorded.

Engagement tier: regulated — the ten boxes of this page are the complete set for this tier.

Claim boundary: 'coverage' reads as reach, tied to the OpenSignal coverage-experience measure, never speed, reliability, quality. Elitza Georgieva coordinates Legal and Regulatory Affairs clearance for all claims and public wording before release. Local strategic approval runs Elitza Georgieva to Malina Chavdarova to Asen Velikov, with Iva Gajić giving United Group approval for divestment-sensitive, group-reputation-facing and major public corporate moments.

Concept boundary: The fixed concept is useful daily digital life proven from the household outward. In public, Vivacom should show it through real service, customer, place and institution proof rather than proclaim it as total leadership.

## Executive summary (2–3 lines)

This strategy speaks first to Maya, the existing customer who judges Vivacom through daily service, bills, app payments, outages and help.

The strongest route is to make daily digital life work from the household outward, using fixed internet, television, reach through OpenSignal coverage-experience proof, and customer help as one visible relationship.

The idea can then serve employees, business buyers, municipalities, regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders without becoming a broad leadership claim.

## Business & communication objectives (SMART+I)

Communication objective: By 30 June 2027 (the second quarter of 2027), build one warmer, proof-led Vivacom corporate story that lifts reputation, affinity and preference against the latest Kantar brand tracker baseline, with Net Promoter Score as a secondary signal, by making existing customers re-see Vivacom as useful, positive and part of daily life. Business objective: growth through preference and value in a mature, price-pressured Bulgarian telecoms market, supporting the owners' goal of a strong eventual sale.

## Target audience profile & persona

Target audience profile & persona: Maya is the first believer. She already uses Vivacom and needs reliable service, clear billing, simple help and fewer surprises. The wider audience includes the critical urban audience, Gen Z, employees and future talent, business and public-sector customers, municipalities, regulators, media, government and parent-group stakeholders, described by role and not renamed.

## The strategic approach + one-line positioning

The recommended approach is Make daily digital life work from the household outward. Positioning: Vivacom makes Bulgaria's daily digital life work, from the home to the institution, through proof people can see. Positioning (lead line): One relationship that makes daily digital life work.

**Positioning (lead line).** One relationship that makes daily digital life work.

**Expression options for the person to choose from.** The concept is fixed; the public expression is open. Candidates: “Works where life happens” (daily usefulness), “The home, connected simply” (household relationship), “Proof you can live with” (service evidence). The choice belongs to a person and is tested with the audience before public use.

**It holds only if.** The approach depends on visible operational proof in the moments Maya uses: fixed internet, television, app payments, bills, outages, contract clarity and support. Legal and Regulatory Affairs must clear every public claim under the legal-proof-pair rule before release. If those service moments fail or the claims outrun proof, the position breaks into another warm corporate promise that customers can disprove from their own account experience.

## Core narrative & 3–5 key messages

Core narrative: Vivacom should not ask people to admire its size. It should show how one useful relationship keeps the home connected, entertainment working, reach visible through OpenSignal coverage-experience proof, and help easier to manage.

Key message 1: Vivacom is strongest when it proves what customers use every day.

Key message 2: Fixed internet and television make the home the first proof point.

Key message 3: Coverage-experience proof means reach, not speed, reliability or quality.

Key message 4: Service moments decide whether the warmer story is believed.

Key message 5: The same proof logic extends to business, public-sector and employee audiences.

## Proof points / supporting evidence

The Approved Brief names existing customers as the primary first-believer audience and says Vivacom under-indexes on warmth. ICLG reports Vivacom at 39.4% of fixed internet subscribers and about 60% of pay-TV subscribers in 2024. OpenSignal says Vivacom dominated coverage experience in January 2026, while A1 was fastest and Yettel led reliability and time on network. The Research & Insight Pack records app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract penalties, outages and data-protection pressure as visible friction.

## Channel strategy (PESO)

PESO means paid, earned, shared and owned media. The approach should lead with earned media because corporate reputation needs third-party proof, then use owned service channels, shared customer proof and selective paid support to repeat the same story.

**Why this leads.** Earned media leads because the gap is trust, not awareness. Paid, shared and owned channels can repeat and deepen the story, but they cannot by themselves make a proof-led corporate role credible.

## Campaign timeline & phases

The rollout dates are not established. The phasing should move from proof lock, to internal alignment, to earned-led launch, to service-channel reinforcement, to quarterly measurement review.

**The phasing spine.** 1) Lock the proof and claim boundaries. 2) Align leaders and internal teams. 3) Launch through earned proof. 4) Reinforce through owned service channels. 5) Review the tracker and friction signals.

## Success metrics & KPIs

Primary measures are reputation, affinity and preference in the Kantar brand tracker. Secondary measures are Net Promoter Score, message recall tied to named proof, quality of earned attention, customer-friction themes, and employee belief. Targets are set once the latest tracker wave and launch baseline are confirmed.

## Budget allocation summary · risk mitigation

The budget is not established and must be proposed by United Partners. The main risks are overclaim, customer friction, sale sensitivity, legal clearance, data and cyber pressure, and the old BTK frame. Crisis-and-issues management runs through the strategy, so every public claim needs proof and a cleared response line.

**Issues preparedness.** Under crisis-and-issues management pressure, the approach holds by narrowing every claim to what can be proved and by treating service friction as part of the story, not a side risk. If an issue rises, Vivacom can answer in the same terms: what happened, who it affects, what proof supports the response, and what changes for customers.

# The Strategy Blueprint cascade

Everything in line of sight: business objective → communication objective → strategic approach → narrative → messages → pillars → platform → tactics → KPIs.

**Business objective.** Growth through preference and value in a mature, price-pressured Bulgarian telecoms market, supporting the owners' goal of a strong eventual sale.

**Communication objective (SMART+I).** By 30 June 2027 (the second quarter of 2027), build one warmer, proof-led Vivacom corporate story that lifts reputation, affinity and preference against the latest Kantar brand tracker baseline, with Net Promoter Score as a secondary signal, by making existing customers re-see Vivacom as useful, positive and part of daily life.

**How it traces.** The communication objective delivers the business objective by using reputation, affinity and preference to support choice and value, while pricing, investment, competition and regulation remain outside communications control.

# The decision rule

If a message does not show how Vivacom makes a real customer, household, workplace or public-service relationship work with named proof, it does not ship, it does not belong.

The team's day-to-day test for whether a message belongs.

# The options it was chosen from

Weak strategy is the first plausible approach written up confidently. These are the alternatives and how each scored.

## Option 1 — Make daily digital life work from the household outward

**Shape.** Reposition

**Direction.** GET Maya and the wider audiences Vivacom serves WHO see separate services and service friction TO see one useful digital relationship BY showing fixed internet, television, reach through OpenSignal coverage-experience proof, and help working together in daily life.

**Positioning.** Vivacom makes Bulgaria's daily digital life work, from the home to the institution, through proof people can see.

| Fit | It resolves the insight's tension because it starts with the household relationship and still serves the wider national role objective. |
| Distinctiveness | It is hard for A1 or Yettel to copy because it joins fixed internet, television, reach through OpenSignal coverage-experience proof, and service touchpoints in one paid relationship. |
| Feasibility | Vivacom can do it because the evidence already supports fixed internet strength, pay-TV strength, coverage-experience reach, and visible customer-service touchpoints. |
| Durability | It can last through a year and a bad news cycle if service proof remains visible and claims stay narrow. |

## Option 2 — Win warmth through service proof before reputation claims

**Shape.** Close the trust gap **Direction.** GET Maya WHO judges Vivacom through bills, app payments, outages, support and contract clarity TO believe Vivacom is becoming easier to live with BY making service fixes the first proof in the story. **Positioning.** Vivacom earns warmth by making the customer relationship clearer and easier to manage. **Rejected —** It is too narrow because it turns the corporate strategy into a service-recovery story.

## Option 3 — Turn national scale into local proof

**Shape.** Own the tension **Direction.** GET customers, employees, business buyers, municipalities, regulators and media WHO see Vivacom as large and active TO see a useful national role BY showing named Bulgarian outcomes in homes, workplaces, schools and local services. **Positioning.** Vivacom turns national scale into useful local outcomes. **Rejected —** It is too easy to pull back into scale, infrastructure and market-power scrutiny.

# UP's recommendation

**Recommended.** Make daily digital life work from the household outward

It beats the others because it has the best fit with the household insight, the strongest distinctiveness against A1 and Yettel, the clearest available proof, and the most durable route through issues pressure. It also keeps the national role without turning scale into the message.

**Coverage.** Vivacom serves consumer, business, enterprise and public-sector customers. The idea starts with Maya at home, then uses the same proof logic for employees, business buyers, municipalities, regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders: show the useful relationship, prove the service, clear the claim.

**Why not the others.** Win warmth through service proof before reputation claims — It is too narrow because it turns the corporate strategy into a service-recovery story. Turn national scale into local proof — It is too easy to pull back into scale, infrastructure and market-power scrutiny.

The recommendation is United Partners'. The choice below stays open until a person makes it.

# Open — waiting on a person

- **Which approach do we take?** — not yet decided; no owner recorded.
- **Which public expression?** — “Works where life happens”, “The home, connected simply”, “Proof you can live with” — tested with the audience before public use; no owner recorded.

compose-big-idea.output:
# The Creative Big Idea

Built through the IdeaHaus method — creativity with structure. A Big Idea is the single organising thought that makes an audience feel something and act, and that a whole programme of work can hang from for years. It is the elevated purpose; a tactic is the activity that serves it. The most common creative failure is presenting the second dressed as the first.

12 candidates were generated and 3 were marked as tactics rather than ideas. 3 are built out below.

**No idea has been chosen.** The volume gives the creative spark and the taste to a person, and no owner is recorded.

## The elevated objective

**What the client asked for.** Vivacom needs a warmer corporate story for existing customers who judge the brand through home internet, television, mobile coverage, bills, app payments, outages and help.

**The value we add.** United Partners turns the story away from corporate scale and into one proof-led household relationship that can also travel to employees, businesses, municipalities, regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders.

**Elevated (NEED + VALUE = POWER).** Make Vivacom the name people use when they talk about daily digital life working across the home, the workplace and the public services they rely on.

**Result-back (the movie ending).** On the day the work has succeeded, Maya does not repeat a corporate promise; she points to her own home and says the internet, television, coverage and help now feel like one relationship she can live with. Employers, municipalities and media then use the same proof pattern when they describe what Vivacom makes possible.

## The insights

**Existing customers will not warm to Vivacom because it is large; they may warm to Vivacom if one household relationship works across fixed internet, pay TV, coverage and customer help.** (empirical) — The approved brief, ICLG fixed internet and pay-TV figures, OpenSignal January 2026 coverage-experience findings, and the recorded customer-friction evidence.

| T | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| True | Pass: the evidence supports Vivacom's household strength and the warmth gap. |
| Tacit | Pass: it names the defended space that A1 and Yettel cannot answer as cleanly. |
| Touches the heart | Partial: it needs customer-language testing before the public line is final. |
| Tension | Pass: it joins Vivacom's proof with the service moments that can disprove it. |
| Triggers action | Pass: it creates a clear test for every message: prove the household relationship or cut it. |

**Warmth will not come from softer language; it will come when customers feel that the same company is accountable for the connected day they already pay for.** (intuitive) — Reasoning from the tension between functional strength and customer friction in bills, app payments, outages, support and contract clarity.

| T | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| True | Conditional: it fits the evidence, but audience testing must confirm whether customers describe accountability in these terms. |
| Tacit | Pass: it exposes the hidden reason a functional leader can still feel cold. |
| Touches the heart | Pass: it speaks to fewer surprises and someone taking responsibility. |
| Tension | Pass: it turns service friction from a side risk into the belief test. |
| Triggers action | Pass: it directs teams to make service proof visible inside the story. |

## The three built out

A true Big Idea is also: about the brand's purpose/benefit; stands out in its category; radically opens hearts and minds; creates movement.

### So You Can

**In one sentence.** Vivacom proves its value by showing what people can do when home internet, television, coverage and help work together.

**The elevated purpose.** Move Vivacom from a company people assess by size to a relationship people judge by what it enables in daily life.

**Why it works.** It presents the agreed platform in plain terms for the reader, supported only by the stated evidence: fixed internet share, pay-TV strength, OpenSignal coverage-experience proof and visible service touchpoints.

**The movement it creates.** People, businesses and institutions answer the same prompt: show what Vivacom helps someone do, then prove the service relationship behind it.

**Why it meets the IdeaHaus bar.** It meets the IdeaHaus bar because it is about the brand benefit, opens hearts through enabled lives, creates movement through the prompt 'so you can', and stands apart from speed-only or reliability-only category frames.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| Simple | Pass: the line is short, active and easy to repeat. |
| Shareable | Pass: people can complete the phrase with their own daily use, from homework to public-service access. |
| Scalable | Pass: it can stretch from households to businesses and municipalities without changing the core thought. |
| Memorable | Pass: the phrase has a clear rhythm and a useful unfinished shape. |
| Ownable | Conditional: Vivacom can own it only when each use carries the fixed internet, pay-TV, coverage-experience or service proof competitors cannot combine in the same way. |
| Persuasive | Pass: it turns proof into a human outcome rather than asking people to admire infrastructure. |

### The Invisible Thread

**In one sentence.** Vivacom shows the quiet relationship that holds a household's digital day together.

**The elevated purpose.** Make people feel the value of Vivacom not as a network claim, but as the continuity behind ordinary moments that would break without it.

**Why it works.** It gives emotional force to the household strategy and lets the work show connection, entertainment, reach and help as one lived pattern.

**The movement it creates.** People start looking for the invisible thread in their own day: the video call that held, the match that played, the payment that cleared, the help that solved the issue.

**Why it meets the IdeaHaus bar.** It meets the IdeaHaus bar because it radically opens hearts, builds a recognisable asset, and can create movement when every story reveals the proof behind a working day.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| Simple | Pass: the image is clear and does not need technical explanation. |
| Shareable | Pass: the thread gives customers and partners an easy way to point to connected moments. |
| Scalable | Pass: it can run through homes, workplaces, schools and local services. |
| Memorable | Pass: the phrase creates a visual asset that can repeat across channels. |
| Ownable | Partial: the metaphor is not owned by Vivacom by itself, so ownership depends on tying it to Vivacom's specific proof combination. |
| Persuasive | Pass: it makes an emotional idea concrete through named daily moments. |

### One Home, One Hand To Hold

**In one sentence.** Vivacom makes one accountable household relationship visible across connection, entertainment, reach and help.

**The elevated purpose.** Turn warmth into a lived feeling of accountability, where the customer knows who helps when digital life has to work.

**Why it works.** It addresses the tension in the insight: Vivacom has household proof, but customers judge that proof through bills, app payments, outages, support and contract clarity.

**The movement it creates.** Customers demand one relationship that is easier to manage, while Vivacom teams use the same standard to decide which messages, fixes and proof points deserve attention.

**Why it meets the IdeaHaus bar.** It meets the IdeaHaus bar because it is about the benefit, creates movement around accountability, and challenges the category habit of selling separate services.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| Simple | Pass: the idea is direct and human. |
| Shareable | Partial: it is emotionally clear, but the phrase may need testing in Bulgarian customer language before public use. |
| Scalable | Conditional: it works strongest in the household and needs careful translation for business and public-sector audiences. |
| Memorable | Pass: the image of one hand gives the idea a human asset. |
| Ownable | Pass if proved: A1 can answer with speed and Yettel with reliability, but neither has the same fixed internet, pay-TV, coverage-experience and household-service proof combination. |
| Persuasive | Pass: it faces service friction instead of pretending warmth can come from tone alone. |

## The volume it came from

Creativity without structure is chaos. Every candidate below names the trainer that produced it, and whether it is really an idea or a tactic — the mayonnaise-versus-sandwich test.

| candidate | trainer | idea or tactic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| So You Can | Movement | idea |
| The Invisible Thread | Random Entry | idea |
| One Home, One Hand To Hold | Provocation | idea |
| Proof You Can Live With | Challenge Idea | idea |
| The Home Becomes The Headline | Challenge Idea | idea |
| Make The Bill Part Of The Promise | Provocation | tactic |
| Every Room Has A Reason | Random Entry | idea |
| From Coverage To Care | Movement | idea |
| The Day Without Digital Friction | Provocation | tactic |
| Stop Selling Networks, Start Holding Households | Challenge Idea | idea |
| The Vivacom Household Test | Movement | tactic |
| Where Help Is Part Of Connection | Random Entry | idea |

## The six IdeaHaus steps, as applied

1. Internalize the strategy — It is based on the approved household-outward strategy, the claim boundary for coverage, and the platform and launch approach the parties have agreed to use.
2. Result-back thinking — Started with Maya and wider audiences actively using Vivacom proof in their own words, not with a brand image result.
3. Embrace insights — Used the WHO truths that Maya wants reliable service, clear billing, simple help and fewer surprises (empirical), and that warmth grows when one household relationship feels accountable (intuitive).
4. Elevate the objectives — Raised the ask from improving warmth to making Vivacom central to the conversations about daily digital life working.
5. Focused ideation — We used Random Entry, Provocation, Challenge Idea and Movement to build on the idea you had already approved in writing, rather than replace it.
6. Validate against the Big Idea Criteria — Tested each built idea for simplicity, shareability, scale, memory, ownership and persuasion, with ownership marked conditional where proof must carry it.

## Validation against the IdeaHaus Big Idea Criteria

The eight criteria, applied to the recommended direction. Where a criterion is only partly met, it is marked so — the check must discriminate.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| About the brand's purpose/benefit | The agreed direction is to explain what Vivacom enables in daily digital life, not to focus on corporate size. |
| Stands out in its category | Pass: it moves away from the speed and reliability battleground and into Vivacom's household proof combination. |
| Radically opens heart & mind | Partial: The Invisible Thread has emotional power, but the language still needs customer testing before it can be treated as heart-opened rather than agency-felt. |
| Simple | Pass: So You Can gives the platform one repeatable human structure. |
| Scalable | Pass: the same proof logic can move from home to workplace, municipality and institution. |
| Recognisable, memorable asset | Pass: The Invisible Thread can become a visual and narrative asset across launch work. |
| Creates movement | Pass: it asks people, businesses and institutions to show what Vivacom helps them do and to demand proof behind the claim. |
| Shareable, any-size screen | Conditional: the platform is screen-native, but executions must keep each story short enough to work in service channels, social posts and earned-media proof. |

**The claim guardrail still holds.** The idea can be big, but every claim must stay narrow, cleared and proved. Coverage means reach through the OpenSignal coverage-experience measure, not speed, reliability or quality; fixed internet, pay TV and service claims must use the evidence already named or new evidence cleared before release. A bigger idea raises the proof standard because more people will test it against their own bills, app payments, outages, support and contracts.

## Two conditions carried into execution

1 · **Proof Before Expression.** Every public execution must show the named household, service, business or public-use proof before it asks the audience to accept the feeling.

2 · **Human Altitude Holder.** Maria Bengtsson holds the emotional altitude of So You Can and The Invisible Thread as the work becomes claims, assets, scripts and service-channel messages.


## The Big Idea

One of the three above becomes the Big Idea. Which one is not recorded here, because the volume gives that choice to a person.

## Open — waiting on a person

- **Which idea has the heart?** — not yet chosen; no owner recorded.

big-idea-gate.output: Passed: it is an elevated purpose and not a tactic; it passes the six Big Idea Criteria; and a person chooses which idea proceeds.

ledger.rule: it is an elevated purpose and not a tactic; it passes the six Big Idea Criteria; and a person chooses which idea proceeds

compose-message-architecture.output:
# Message Architecture

One connected architecture, not three separate lists. Every message and every pillar traces back to the one story; anything that does not, does not belong.

**Waiting on an owner.** The story's truth and its tension belong to a person, and no owner has approved them in writing yet.

## Rebuilt from the Big Idea

This architecture is built from the Big Idea the strategist decided — So You Can, launched through The Invisible Thread — not from the nearest provable frame. The idea's role is the spine; the first-believer audience is the first proof of it, not the whole story.

## The narrative

**World.** Bulgaria's digital life is judged in ordinary moments: the home internet works, the television plays, the bill is clear, the app payment goes through, and help is there when something breaks.

**Tension.** People need connection to stay out of the way so they can live, work, watch, pay, study and stay close to family. Broad telecom claims pull against that need when customers see outages, unclear bills, contract disputes, app criticism or slow help.

**Resolution.** The story resolves when Vivacom proves The Invisible Thread from the household outward: one useful relationship that connects home, entertainment, reach and help through proof people can see.

**Our role.** Vivacom's role is to keep The Invisible Thread working, So You Can do what matters most to them, in the best possible way.

### In the UP template

**We believe in a world where…** people should be able to rely on digital life without thinking about the systems behind it.

**We know…** customers do not warm to size alone. They believe the company when the bill, app, television, coverage and help work in real life.

**So we make sure…** the story starts with the home, uses OpenSignal coverage-experience proof only as reach, and treats service moments as proof of the promise.

**Which is why we…** tell The Invisible Thread: Vivacom keeps daily digital life working from the household outward, So You Can.

### Compressed

**Trailer.** Maya is not waiting for a bigger telecom claim. She is trying to keep her home connected, her television working, her bill clear and her family close.

**Tweet.** Vivacom keeps The Invisible Thread working from the home outward: fixed internet, television, coverage-experience reach and help in one relationship, So You Can get on with daily life.

## Key messages

The six-type Messaging Architecture — Awareness, Relevance, Emotion, Logic, Action, Commitment — under one umbrella message. Each message laddered with the Trident: 1° umbrella claim → 2° supporting pillar → 3° killer fact.

| message | audience | type | pillar | 1° umbrella | 2° supporting | 3° killer fact | do not say |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vivacom keeps The Invisible Thread working, So You Can get on with daily life. | Existing customers, with Maya as the first believer. | Emotion | The Invisible Thread starts at home. | Vivacom keeps The Invisible Thread working, So You Can get on with daily life. | The home is where customers first judge the relationship: fixed internet, television, app payments, bills, outages and help. | The approved brief names existing customers as the primary first-believer audience and says Vivacom under-indexes on warmth. | Do not say service friction is a side issue. |
| Vivacom is strongest when it proves the household relationship people already use. | Consumer customers and the critical urban audience. | Relevance | The household relationship is Vivacom's first proof. | Vivacom is strongest when it proves the household relationship people already use. | Fixed internet, pay television, coverage-experience reach and service touchpoints make one paid daily relationship. | The International Comparative Legal Guides report Vivacom at 39.4% of fixed internet subscribers and about 60% of pay-television subscribers in 2024. | Do not say Vivacom is the best network, fastest network or most reliable network in Bulgaria. |
| Vivacom can show reach through coverage-experience proof, not through broad network claims. | Regulators, media, government and parent-group stakeholders. | Logic | Reach is proved carefully, not claimed broadly. | Vivacom can show reach through coverage-experience proof, not through broad network claims. | Coverage-experience proof must mean reach only, with every public claim cleared by Legal and Regulatory Affairs. | OpenSignal says Vivacom dominated coverage experience in January 2026, while A1 was fastest and Yettel led reliability and time on network. | Do not say coverage means speed, reliability or quality. · Do not say Vivacom is the best network, fastest network or most reliable network in Bulgaria. |
| Every service moment is where The Invisible Thread is either proved or broken in public. | Employees, service teams and leaders. | Commitment | Service moments prove the idea in public. | Every service moment is where The Invisible Thread is either proved or broken in public. | Bills, app payments, outages, contract clarity and support must sit inside the story because customers use them to judge the promise. | The Research and Insight Pack records app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract penalties, outages and data-protection pressure as visible friction. | Do not say service friction is a side issue. |
| The same proof logic carries from the home to workplaces, municipalities and public services. | Business buyers, public-sector customers, municipalities and employees. | Action | The proof travels from household to institution. | The same proof logic carries from the home to workplaces, municipalities and public services. | Vivacom should show useful relationships in real homes, workplaces, schools, institutions and local services. | The Strategy One-Pager states that the idea starts with Maya at home, then extends the same proof logic to employees, business buyers, municipalities, regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders. | Do not say Vivacom is total technology leader or ask people to admire its size. |

## Communications pillars

The few enduring territories, each tracing to the narrative, balanced across Hero ~20%, Hub ~60%, Hygiene ~20%.

### The Invisible Thread starts at home.

**Traces to.** role

**Audiences.** Existing customers, with Maya as the first believer.

**Carries the message.** Vivacom keeps The Invisible Thread working, So You Can get on with daily life.

**Stakeholder track.** consumer affinity

**Proof to validate.** Audience testing must show that existing customers find the household route more believable than national progress or broad best-network routes.

**Do not say.** Do not say service friction is a side issue.

**Hero.** A named Maya story that shows one felt moment: a clear bill, working television, simple help or staying connected to family.

**Hub.** Recurring household proof stories across fixed internet, television, app payment, billing and help.

**Hygiene.** Short service explainers, claim notes and response lines for common customer questions.

**Story types.** Evergreen, Real-time Reactive

### The household relationship is Vivacom's first proof.

**Traces to.** resolution

**Audiences.** Consumer customers and the critical urban audience.

**Carries the message.** Vivacom is strongest when it proves the household relationship people already use.

**Stakeholder track.** brand consistency

**Proof to validate.** Fixed internet share, pay-television share, household use and customer-service evidence must be checked before this pillar leads.

**Do not say.** Do not say Vivacom is the best network, fastest network or most reliable network in Bulgaria.

**Hero.** One clear household proof story that joins internet, television, reach and help.

**Hub.** Customer and service stories that show useful digital life working across the home.

**Hygiene.** Product proof, customer-service facts and claim-approved lines for paid, owned and shared use.

**Story types.** Evergreen, Seasonal

### Reach is proved carefully, not claimed broadly.

**Traces to.** tension

**Audiences.** Regulators, media, government and parent-group stakeholders.

**Carries the message.** Vivacom can show reach through coverage-experience proof, not through broad network claims.

**Stakeholder track.** earned proof

**Proof to validate.** Legal and Regulatory Affairs must clear each claim, and the OpenSignal coverage-experience source must support the exact wording.

**Do not say.** Do not say coverage means speed, reliability or quality. · Do not say Vivacom is the best network, fastest network or most reliable network in Bulgaria.

**Hero.** A claim-safe proof story about reach, with the OpenSignal coverage-experience boundary visible.

**Hub.** Explainers, media briefings and leader lines that separate reach from speed, reliability and quality.

**Hygiene.** Approved claim language, source notes and response lines for competitor comparisons.

**Story types.** Evergreen, Real-time Reactive

### Service moments prove the idea in public.

**Traces to.** tension

**Audiences.** Existing customers, employees, service teams and leaders.

**Carries the message.** Every service moment is where The Invisible Thread is either proved or broken in public.

**Stakeholder track.** owned service channels

**Proof to validate.** Vivacom must validate which service fixes or service standards can be shown before this pillar leads publicly.

**Do not say.** Do not say service friction is a side issue.

**Hero.** A visible service moment that shows what happened, who it affected and what changed for customers.

**Hub.** Practical service stories about bills, app payments, outages, support and contract clarity.

**Hygiene.** Plain-language customer updates, service notices and issue response lines.

**Story types.** Real-time Reactive, Evergreen

### The proof travels from household to institution.

**Traces to.** role

**Audiences.** Business buyers, public-sector customers, municipalities, employees and parent-group stakeholders.

**Carries the message.** The same proof logic carries from the home to workplaces, municipalities and public services.

**Stakeholder track.** partner ecosystem

**Proof to validate.** Business, public-sector and municipal examples must be named, current and cleared before this pillar leads.

**Do not say.** Do not say Vivacom is total technology leader or ask people to admire its size.

**Hero.** One named workplace, municipality or public-service proof story that shows useful digital life beyond the home.

**Hub.** Case stories from business customers, local services, schools, institutions and employees.

**Hygiene.** Case facts, partner approvals, leader talking points and claim-safe evidence notes.

**Story types.** Evergreen, Seasonal

**Market weighting.** B2C — Earned, shared and community tracks lead because the idea asks people to feel The Invisible Thread in daily life, not just hear a corporate claim. Consumer affinity and brand consistency are weighted because Maya's household experience is the first proof, and the same proof must then travel to employees, business buyers, municipalities, regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders.

## Do-not-say guardrails

| do not say | why |
| --- | --- |
| Do not say coverage means speed, reliability or quality. | The claim boundary says coverage reads as reach, tied to the OpenSignal coverage-experience measure. |
| Do not say Vivacom is the best network, fastest network or most reliable network in Bulgaria. | OpenSignal says Vivacom dominated coverage experience, while A1 was fastest and Yettel led reliability and time on network. |
| Do not say Vivacom is total technology leader or ask people to admire its size. | The strategy says Vivacom should show real service, customer, place and institution proof rather than proclaim total leadership or size. |
| Do not say service friction is a side issue. | The material records app reviews, Trustpilot criticism, contract penalties, outages and data-protection pressure as visible friction that decides whether the story is believed. |
| Do not use the old BTK frame as the story. | The Strategy One-Pager names the old BTK frame as a risk, so the story should prove today's useful relationship instead of arguing with history. |

## The Content Strategy Cascade

Narrative → Themes → Stories → Sequencing.

## The content balance

Described at all three levels without the proportions, a pillar reads as three equal commitments. It is not — the middle carries the programme.

| level | share and what it is |
| --- | --- |
| Hero | ~20% — the few big moments |
| Hub | ~60% — ongoing content that builds audience and demonstrates the pillars |
| Hygiene | ~20% — the always-on answers people actually search for |


## Open — waiting on a person

- **Is this story true, and is its tension real?** — waiting on a person; no owner recorded.
- **Are these messages and their proof approved?** — waiting on a person; no owner recorded.
- **Are the do-not-say lines set?** — waiting on a person; no owner recorded.
- **Are these the pillars?** — waiting on a person; no owner recorded.

narrative-gate.output: Passed: everything ladders to the one narrative — no orphan messages, no pillar that does not trace back to the story.

ledger.rule: everything ladders to the one narrative — no orphan messages, no pillar that does not trace back to the story

compose-communications-platform.output:
# The Communications Platform

An architecture, not a list. If the channels could each belong to a different strategy, this would be a list.

**No platform has been chosen.** The candidates and their tests are below; the choice, and the judgement of what is genuinely ownable, belong to a person.

## Candidate platforms, against the five criteria

### Candidate 1 — So You Can: The Invisible Thread

**Why it is ownable.** Vivacom can own this because the evidence connects fixed internet, television, coverage-experience reach and service moments into one daily relationship that starts at home.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| Differentiation | It differentiates Vivacom by joining home services, reach and help instead of making a broad network claim. |
| Heritage | It uses Vivacom's current household role and avoids making the old BTK (the former state-monopoly telecom name in Bulgaria) frame the story. |
| Extension | It can extend from homes to workplaces, municipalities and public services through the same proof logic. |
| Competitive advantage | It uses fixed internet share, pay-television share and OpenSignal coverage-experience proof in a way A1 and Yettel cannot copy as one relationship. |
| Durable / global | It can last if service proof stays visible and every coverage claim stays inside the approved reach boundary. |

### Candidate 2 — So You Can: Daily Life Connected

**Why it is ownable.** Vivacom can own this if it shows how the household relationship helps people live, work, watch, pay, study and stay close to family.

| criterion | judgement |
| --- | --- |
| Differentiation | It differentiates Vivacom when it proves useful daily life rather than size, speed or total technology leadership. |
| Heritage | It fits the present Vivacom relationship better than the inherited telecom history. |
| Extension | It gives consumer, employee, business, public-sector and municipal audiences one shared logic. |
| Competitive advantage | It is credible because the proof starts with fixed internet, pay television, coverage-experience reach and service touchpoints. |
| Durable / global | It can travel, but it needs local proof in each market or audience before it leads. |

## PESO, orchestrated around one insight

PESO (Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned) is the channel architecture the platform orchestrates against. Earned-led, because for corporate reputation third-party credibility is what builds trust.

| channel | its role here | the volume's role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paid | Paid media supports the platform selectively. It drives people to owned proof, then amplifies earned stories and shared customer proof once claims are cleared. | Controlled reach and action — support, selective |
| Earned | Earned media leads because corporate reputation needs third-party proof. This platform is earned-led because the trust gap cannot be solved by paid reach alone. | Third-party credibility and validation — the reputation engine, and it leads |
| Shared | Shared media carries customer, employee and community proof. It spreads earned stories and points people back to owned explanations when service questions appear. | Participation and advocacy — support |
| Owned | Owned media holds the full proof: service updates, explainers, case stories, claim notes and customer help. Owned content feeds influencers, employees and media with the same approved story. | Depth, education and conversion — the foundation |

## The 4C integrated programming model

Unifying Human Insight → Find the Right Moment → Deploy the Right Channels → Engage Influencers → Develop Compelling Content → Evaluate & Recalibrate.

## The engagement model

How an audience is moved, stage by stage. The stages are not interchangeable: nobody is mobilised who was never engaged, and advocacy asked for before connection is noise.

| stage | what it is for |
| --- | --- |
| Align / Engage | reach the audience where they already are, on something they already care about |
| Develop / Enhance | deepen what they understand, so the relationship survives one message |
| Connect / Advocate | give them a reason and a means to say it themselves |
| Mobilise / Amplify | turn that into visible action at a scale that changes the picture |

**Underneath all four, always on.** Campaigns punctuate this baseline; they are not the baseline. A plan of bursts with nothing underneath cannot hold a reputation between them.

- **Conversation Management loop.** listen, triage, respond and escalate on what is already being said, every day, whether or not a campaign is running
- **The Observatory newsroom.** watch the environment for the moments worth entering, and be ready to publish into them before they close

## Activation Cards

No tactic goes on the calendar until it is a card, and every card traces up to an audience, a message and a pillar.

### Card 1 — The Invisible Thread at Home

**Insight.** Existing customers judge Vivacom first through the moments inside the home: internet, television, bills, app payments, outages and help.

**Idea.** Show one named household story under The Invisible Thread, So You Can, where Vivacom helps daily life continue without asking people to admire the system behind it.

**Engagement.** Launch the story through earned media, then drive readers to owned proof that explains the services and support behind the moment.

**Outcome.** Existing customers see Vivacom as useful and warmer because the claim is shown through daily household proof.

**Line of sight.** Existing customers, with Maya as the first believer. · Vivacom keeps The Invisible Thread working, So You Can get on with daily life. · The Invisible Thread starts at home.

**Channel.** Earned, owned, shared and selective paid support.  ·  **KPI (key performance indicator).** Message recall tied to the household proof, quality of earned attention, owned proof-page visits and customer-friction themes.  ·  **Phase.** We will lead the launch through earned channels once you have approved the proof points and claim boundaries in writing.

### Card 2 — Household Proof Series

**Insight.** Vivacom is most believable when it proves the relationship customers already use every day.

**Idea.** Publish a recurring hub series that connects fixed internet, television, coverage-experience reach and help as one household relationship under The Invisible Thread.

**Engagement.** Use owned channels as the home for the series, feed stories to influencers and use paid media to drive people to the proof.

**Outcome.** The household relationship becomes the repeatable proof of So You Can, not a one-off launch story.

**Line of sight.** Consumer customers and the critical urban audience. · Vivacom is strongest when it proves the household relationship people already use. · The household relationship is Vivacom's first proof.

**Channel.** Owned, shared, earned and paid.  ·  **KPI.** Repeat visits to owned stories, engagement with shared posts, influencer use of approved proof and tracker movement on affinity.  ·  **Phase.** Always-on after launch.

### Card 3 — Reach, Clearly Explained

**Insight.** Coverage-experience proof can support reach, but it cannot support claims about speed, reliability or overall quality.

**Idea.** Create claim-cleared explainers and media lines that show how Vivacom proves reach while keeping The Invisible Thread inside the approved evidence.

**Engagement.** Brief media and stakeholders with the source boundary visible, then amplify the cleared explanation through owned and paid channels.

**Outcome.** Regulators, media and parent-group stakeholders see a disciplined proof story instead of a broad network claim.

**Line of sight.** Regulators, media, government and parent-group stakeholders. · Vivacom can show reach through coverage-experience proof, not through broad network claims. · Reach is proved carefully, not claimed broadly.

**Channel.** Earned, owned and paid amplification.  ·  **KPI.** Share of earned coverage that uses the approved reach wording, absence of unsupported best-network claims and Legal and Regulatory Affairs clearance status.  ·  **Phase.** Proof lock, launch and issues response.

### Card 4 — Service Moment Response Lines

**Insight.** A service issue can prove or break The Invisible Thread in public.

**Idea.** Build plain-language service updates that say what happened, who it affects, what Vivacom is doing and what changes for customers.

**Engagement.** Use owned service channels first, then support with shared updates and earned response lines when an issue becomes public.

**Outcome.** Vivacom treats service friction as part of the promise and gives customers clear answers when the promise is tested.

**Line of sight.** Existing customers, employees, service teams and leaders. · Every service moment is where The Invisible Thread is either proved or broken in public. · Service moments prove the idea in public.

**Channel.** Owned, shared and earned.  ·  **KPI.** Speed of approved response, customer understanding, issue-theme reduction and sentiment around service updates.  ·  **Phase.** Always-on and real-time reactive.

## The Communications Plan

### The platform idea and why it is ownable

The platform is So You Can, launched through The Invisible Thread. It shows how Vivacom keeps daily digital life working from the household outward, so people can live, work, watch, pay, study and stay close to family.

### Rollout strategies and phasing

The rollout should move from proof lock, to internal alignment, to earned-led launch, to owned service reinforcement, to quarterly measurement review. Dates are not established in the material.

### Target audiences prioritised, each with its channels and tactics

The first audience is existing customers, with Maya as the first believer. The wider audience includes the critical urban audience, Gen Z, employees and future talent, business and public-sector customers, municipalities, regulators, media, government and parent-group stakeholders.

### The PESO channel architecture, earned-led and integrated

Earned media leads the corporate reputation work. Owned service channels run always-on with explainers, updates, claim notes and proof stories, while the newsroom monitors service moments, prepares cleared response lines and turns proof into media-ready stories; the material does not establish the newsroom's staffing model.

### The tactics as Activation Cards

The calendar should carry a small number of hero moments, a larger hub of recurring household and service proof, and hygiene content that answers real customer questions. Each tactic must trace to an audience, message and pillar before it runs.

### The 12-month content calendar

The campaign dates are not established. The practical sequence is proof and claim clearance first, internal alignment second, earned launch third, always-on owned and shared reinforcement fourth, then quarterly review against tracker, Net Promoter Score and friction signals.

### The integrated plan and messages, sequenced

The story starts at home because that is where customers judge Vivacom first. It then extends to reach, service moments, workplaces, municipalities and public services only when the proof is named, current and cleared.

## The Pyramid of Influence

The voices who carry the story, from the top down.

| level | who they are |
| --- | --- |
| Professional Influencers | journalists, analysts, named experts |
| The Power Middle | semi-pro creators, sector voices |
| Super Fans & Employees | the people who already carry it without being asked |
| Fans & Followers | the audience that amplifies what it already believes |

For corporate reputation the highest-value influencers are usually credible third parties — analysts, editors, respected alumni or partners — and employees as advocates.

## The pull-through line of sight

Vision / Position → Brand Expression → Go-to-Market → Communications Programs.

## Open — waiting on a person

- **Which platform do we build?** — not yet decided; no owner recorded.

**Strategy recap.** The plan is earned-led because corporate reputation needs third-party proof. ## C · The messages & assets

### Message tracks

#### Existing customers, with Maya as the first believer
